Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com
Doc no. POL-QM-05  ·  Rev 3  ·  Date 03/15/2025  ·  Owner: DER Program Office

Queue Management & Withdrawal Policy
Applies to:  All DER Interconnection Program applications (≥500 kW) administered by the DER Program Office.
Supersedes:  POL-QM-05 Rev 2 (07/12/2023).
Owner:  DER Program Office.
Approving Authority:  Manager, Interconnection Studies.

§1  Purpose
This policy sets out the internal procedures by which the DER Program Office administers queue integrity and orderly withdrawal of applications from the active DER interconnection queue. It is intended to ensure that:
(a)applications are closed only on a documented basis;
(b)queue positions are established, retained, and released in a manner consistent with the Company's APUC-filed interconnection tariff (in particular §12.3, §12.4, and §12.6) and with the DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01);
(c)staff processing intake, screening, and case-management actions apply a single, uniform standard when an application appears stalled, abandoned, superseded, or replaced by a subsequent filing at the same site; and
(d)the record supporting each queue action is complete and auditable.
Nothing in this policy modifies the tariff. Where any provision of this policy is read to conflict with the tariff or with an applicable engineering standard, the tariff and the standard control, and the conflict shall be referred to Regulatory Affairs for reconciliation.
§2  Withdrawal upon Customer Request
A stalled or abandoned application is closed only upon receipt of the customer's official withdrawal confirmation, provided in writing by letter or email. Where a new filing is submitted for the same site while a prior application remains open, the program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing; the new application takes its own queue date at time of filing. No queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§2.1  Scope of §2
This §2 governs closure of applications that have not been the subject of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under tariff §12.4. It applies where:
(a)the customer has ceased substantive engagement with the program (whether by prolonged non-response, express indication of intent not to proceed, or otherwise);
(b)the customer or an authorized developer has requested closure of an application without such a notice having issued; or
(c)a new application is filed for the same site (as identified by service address, meter, or point of common coupling) while a prior application for that site remains in the active queue.
§2.2  Form of the Withdrawal Confirmation
To constitute an “official withdrawal confirmation” for purposes of this §2, the writing must:
(a)be from the applicant of record (or from a person whose authority to act for the applicant has been established on the record — e.g., the developer named as the applicant's designated representative on the intake form);
(b)be received by the DER Program Office by letter or email, addressed to der.program@alleniom.com or delivered to the DER Program Office at the letterhead address above;
(c)identify the application by application identifier (PXA-YYYY-NNNN) and site; and
(d)state expressly that the applicant withdraws the identified application.
Neither an oral communication (telephone, meeting, or voicemail), nor a status note recorded by staff, nor the mere filing of a new application at the same site, shall by itself constitute the official withdrawal confirmation required under this §2.
§2.3  Procedure — Stalled or Abandoned Application (Non-Notice Path)
Where staff identify an application within the scope of §2.1(a) or §2.1(b), the case handler shall:
1.Confirm the application's status in the active queue and document the basis for concluding that the application is stalled or abandoned;
2.Prepare and send a written communication (letter or email) to the applicant of record requesting the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation in the form specified in §2.2;
3.Log the request in the case file and in the queue-management system;
4.On receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, close the application and record the closure date, the closure basis (“§2 — customer request”), and the reference to the writing on file; and
5.Preserve the withdrawal writing in the case file in accordance with §4.
Absent receipt of the official withdrawal confirmation, the application shall not be closed under this §2. If the applicant does not provide the confirmation and non-response persists, the case handler may refer the matter for issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §3.
§2.4  Duplicate Filings at the Same Site
Where a new application is filed for the same site while a prior application for that site remains open in the queue:
(a)The DER Program Office shall accept the new application in the ordinary course and shall assign the new application its own queue date determined as of the date the new application is determined to be complete. No queue-date inheritance is permitted between the prior and the new application.
(b)The program shall request the customer's official withdrawal of the prior filing in the form specified in §2.2. That request may be combined with the completeness/acknowledgement communication for the new application.
(c)The prior application shall remain open in the queue until the official withdrawal confirmation is received, or until the prior application is otherwise closed by operation of §3 or under another tariff mechanism. The two applications shall not be merged, consolidated, or treated as continuations of a single filing.
(d)Where the applicant states a preference or expectation that the earlier queue date apply to the new filing, staff shall respond in writing that the new application's queue date is fixed by §12.3 of the tariff and by this §2.4, and that closure of the prior application does not alter the queue date of the new application.
§2.5  Consistency with DIS-01 §7 and Tariff §12.6
Nothing in this §2 authorizes the use of a customer-requested withdrawal to reopen or amend an executed Interconnection Service Agreement. Post-execution changes to material terms of an ISA — including nameplate capacity and point of interconnection — require withdrawal-and-reapplication in accordance with DIS-01 §7 and tariff §12.6. A customer-requested withdrawal in that context establishes a new queue date for the successor application; no queue-date inheritance is permitted.
§3  Deemed Withdrawal (Procedural Restatement of Tariff §12.4)
Following issuance of a formal Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation, if the applicant fails to respond within 30 business days, the application is deemed withdrawn.
§3.1  Relationship to the Tariff
This §3 is a procedural restatement, for internal use, of the deemed-withdrawal mechanism established by tariff §12.4. In the event of any inconsistency between this §3 and §12.4, the tariff controls. Staff shall consult §12.4 for the authoritative statement of the mechanism.
§3.2  Prerequisites to Issuance of a Notice
The DER Program Office shall not issue a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation unless:
(a)the application has been open in the queue and staff have been unable to advance it because of the applicant's non-response or failure to supply required information or documentation;
(b)at least one prior written follow-up has been sent to the applicant identifying the item or items required and requesting response by a stated date; and
(c)the case handler has confirmed that the matter does not fall within the construction-payment default procedure under tariff §12.5, which is a distinct mechanism (project on hold, not withdrawn, while a 30-business-day payment deadline runs).
§3.3  Form and Service of the Notice
Every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall:
(a)be issued in writing on Alleniom Utilities letterhead;
(b)be served by certified mail or by verified electronic delivery, in accordance with tariff §12.4;
(c)identify the application by identifier and site;
(d)state the item(s) requiring response;
(e)state the date of issuance and the date on which the 30 business-day response window expires, computed under §3.4; and
(f)state the consequence of non-response, i.e., that the application shall be deemed withdrawn and closed from the active queue without further action.
§3.4  Computation of 30 Business Days
For purposes of this §3 and of tariff §12.4:
(a)“Business days” excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and federal legal public holidays observed within the response window;
(b)Day 1 is the first business day after the date of issuance stated on the notice;
(c)The following federal holidays observed within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized as non-business days and are not counted:
Holiday | Observed Date
Memorial Day | 05/26/2025
Juneteenth National Independence Day | 06/19/2025
Independence Day | 07/04/2025


(d)Where a response window straddles a federal holiday not listed above, the case handler shall exclude that holiday from the count and document the calculation in the case file.
§3.5  Effect of Non-Response
If the applicant fails to submit a substantive response curing the matter identified in the notice within 30 business days computed under §3.4, the application shall be deemed withdrawn as of the day following expiration of the window. The DER Program Office shall:
(a)mark the application “deemed withdrawn — §12.4” in the queue-management system;
(b)record the notice-issuance date, the expiration date, and the closure date in the withdrawal-notice log; and
(c)preserve the notice, proof of service, and the closure entry in the case file in accordance with §4.
§3.6  Effect of Timely Response
A substantive response received on or before expiration of the 30 business-day window suspends the deemed-withdrawal consequence. The case handler shall evaluate the response and, if the identified matter is cured, release the application to resume processing. If the response is non-substantive or does not cure the identified matter, the case handler shall so document and, if warranted, issue a further follow-up or a subsequent Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation.
§3.7  Non-Substitution
Issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation is not a substitute for the customer-request path under §2, and the customer-request path under §2 is not a substitute for the deemed-withdrawal path under §3. Case handlers shall not use one mechanism to accomplish what should be effected under the other.
§4  Record-Keeping Requirements
§4.1  Case File Contents
For every application closed under §2 or §3, the DER Program Office shall maintain a case file containing, at minimum:
(a)the original application and all completeness/acknowledgement communications;
(b)for §2 closures: the writing (letter or email) requesting official withdrawal confirmation from the applicant; the applicant's official withdrawal confirmation (letter or email) as received; and any related correspondence bearing on the applicant's intent to withdraw;
(c)for §3 closures: the prior follow-up correspondence relied upon under §3.2(b); the Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation as issued; proof of service (certified mail receipt or verified electronic delivery record); the 30 business-day computation worksheet; and any response received;
(d)the queue-management system entry recording the closure basis, closure date, and (for §2 duplicate-filing cases) the queue-date determination applied to the successor application under §2.4(a); and
(e)any related engineering or standards correspondence relied upon in the closure decision.
§4.2  Queue-Management System Entries
Every closure shall be recorded in the queue-management system with:
(a)application identifier and site;
(b)closure basis, expressed as one of: “§2 — customer request (letter)”, “§2 — customer request (email)”, “§2.4 — superseded by successor application”, “§12.4 — deemed withdrawn”, or such other codes as the DER Program Office may prescribe;
(c)closure date;
(d)case handler; and
(e)reference to the writing(s) supporting the closure basis.
§4.3  Withdrawal-Notice Log
The DER Program Office shall maintain a running Withdrawal-Notice Log recording every Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation issued. The log shall include, at minimum: application identifier; site; date of issuance; method of service; response deadline (computed under §3.4); response received (date and disposition, if any); and closure date (if any). The log is subject to periodic reconciliation against the on-hold queue report; unreconciled entries shall be brought to the attention of the Manager, Interconnection Studies.
§4.4  Retention
Case files and log entries shall be retained in accordance with the Company's records retention schedule for regulated interconnection records. Records shall not be purged, redacted, or altered while an application remains open, while a response window under §3 is running, or while the closure is within the period during which reconsideration may be sought.
§4.5  Audit and Reporting
The Manager, Interconnection Studies shall be prepared, on request of Regulatory Affairs, to produce for any closed application: the closure basis; the writing(s) supporting the closure basis; the queue-date determination for any successor application; and, where applicable, the notice, proof of service, and 30 business-day computation. Reports to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission concerning queue closures shall be prepared from the withdrawal-notice log and the queue-management system entries described above.

name: utility-interconnection
description: How utility interconnection, pre-PTO backfeed/energization, witness tests and permission to operate normally work, the reviewer's two-layer check (procedural conditions, then an independent engineering review of the customer's records against the adopted code), walking the operating states, a typical electrical review list, and how a professional determination memo or customer letter is written. Use for any interconnection, energization, PTO, commissioning-approval or utility-reply task.

# Utility interconnection, energization and permission to operate (PTO)
Typical lifecycle: application -> screening / studies -> interconnection agreement (ISA) -> construction
(customer facilities under an electrical permit from the authority having jurisdiction, AHJ; utility facilities
under a work order paid by the customer) -> AHJ final inspection and approval -> utility commissioning (metering,
telemetry/RTU end-to-end test, POI protective device acceptance) -> witness test or documented waiver -> written
PTO. Parallel operation before PTO happens only for a witness test under a switching order.
Pre-PTO backfeed / energization for commissioning: utility energizes the customer's transformer and collection
system with the generators disabled and isolated (inverter disconnects open and locked). Normally requires: an
agreement term allowing it, a written request, AHJ final approval of the work being energized, customer
equipment complete and safe to energize (code-compliant wiring, grounding, overcurrent
protection, labels, disconnects), metering set, switching order.
Reviewer's duties:
- Two separate checks: (1) procedural conditions in the agreement, tariff, standards and permit; (2) an
  independent engineering review of the customer's construction records line by line against the code edition
  the permit adopts and the utility standards. Do this even when the AHJ has passed the work; an approval by
  another party is evidence, not proof. A code non-conformance in the record must be corrected and documented
  before energization/PTO.
- Walk the operating states: before PTO (POI device open), during the requested operation, normal parallel
  operation, after a POI trip or utility outage. In each state ask what is energized, what must remain in
  service, and what must be isolated.
- Functions that must keep working (telemetry and RTU, protection relays, communications, remote control, metering):
  trace each one's power supply back to its source (station service, auxiliary transformer, battery/UPS and its
  autonomy) and check it stays energized in every operating state, including while the POI device is open; a
  confirmation obtained in one operating state does not prove another.
- Equipment that will be energized must comply as installed, whatever the generators are doing: generation being
  disabled does not excuse wiring-method, support, labelling, rating or protection defects in the energized part.
- Every finding, adverse or favourable, opens and quotes the clause it relies on and checks its conditions and
  exceptions (a clause that permits the installation removes an apparent violation; a clause not read cannot support
  "compliant").
- Respect the stated scope; where an out-of-scope item depends on something in scope, review the in-scope part.
- Review electrical construction records by NEC article (the edition the permit adopts), plus the utility's
  interconnection standards: 110 (equipment ratings vs available fault current, working space, enclosure ratings,
  markings); 240 (overcurrent protection); 250 (grounding and bonding, equipment grounding and electrode conductors);
  300/310 (wiring methods for the location, support, burial, ampacity with correction factors and terminal ratings);
  312/314 (cabinets, boxes, enclosures); 690 (PV circuits, dc voltage, disconnects, rapid shutdown, labels); 705
  (interconnected sources: point of connection, busbar and conductor rules, disconnects); 706 (energy storage).
Professional reply / memo:
- First sentence answers the question one way or the other (yes / no / not on that date) with the decisive reason.
- For each obstacle: what it is, the exact requirement (document, clause, edition), the evidence in the record,
  what must be done, by whom (name the customer when it is theirs), whether it can be done before the date, and
  what happens if not. Then the path to "yes" (what to resubmit, who re-inspects).
- Items checked and found acceptable: brief list.
- Internal memo vs external letter: an external letter does not cite internal directives or staff deliberations,
  stays short (1-2 pages), and gives one contact. An internal memo can cite internal procedures.
- Do not call a real obstacle a "confirmation", and do not raise an obstacle you have not verified.
- The tracker item (ticket / work package) mirrors the determination: one line per open item with owner and due date.
Before sending: re-check every cited clause and table value against the source; check dates and notice periods
with a script; check that the answer, the open items and the ticket agree; check names and titles against the
contact directory; check that nothing dated after the "as of" date was used.

name: professional-memo
description: How to write an engineering memo, letter, reply, review response or technical note for a named recipient, written for an expert reader - answer first, basis from the record, every issue with owner and timing, exact scope, signature block, and a correct DOCX file. Use whenever the deliverable is a memo, letter, reply, response, review, disposition or note.

# Professional engineering memo

## Before writing
- Identify: who asked, who will act on the memo, the decision they must take, the "as of" date of the record, and any
  dates in the request (target date, deadline). Note what the request says is OUT of scope and leave it out.
- Gather the record: correspondence (emails, letters, RFIs), applications, studies, test reports, standards, contracts,
  tracking data in project applications. Build a dated timeline of relevant events in `/tmp/ahpele/timeline.md`.
- For each potential issue, find the exact source (document, section, date) and what it requires.
- For go/no-go questions (approve, issue, energise, accept, pay), do not stop at the first favourable reading. Build a checklist of every condition that applies
  (agreements, studies, permits, tests, payments, insurance, notices, deadlines, sign-offs, open correspondence) and
  check each one against the record as of the stated date. Only conclude that nothing blocks the decision after every
  condition has been checked and cited.

## Structure
1. Header: To / From / Date (use the record's "as of" date unless told otherwise) / Subject / project identifiers.
2. **Answer first**: one or two sentences that directly answer the question (yes / no / not yet, by which date), with
   the decisive reason.
3. **Basis**: the facts and requirements the answer rests on, each cited to the record (document, section, date).
4. **Open items** (one per issue): what it is; what requirement it rests on (cite it); what has to be done; who must do
   it (name the party or role, including the customer/applicant when it is theirs); whether it can be done before the
   target date and why; consequence if not.
5. Items reviewed and found acceptable, briefly, so the reader knows they were checked.
6. Scope statement: what this memo does not cover, exactly as the request defines it.
7. Recommendation / next steps with dates.
8. Signature block for the reviewing engineer if the request asks for one (name/title placeholders only where the
   request leaves the signer unnamed; never invent credentials).

## Determinations the reader can check
- Make a list of every question and request in the instruction (asks.md) and answer each one in its own labelled place.
- Each answer states the specific fact and the conclusion in one or two plain sentences: "<thing> is / is not <state>,
  because <fact with value and unit> (<document, section/sheet, date>)". Then give the working.
- When the record does not let you decide a question, say exactly what is missing, who must provide it and what the
  decision is meanwhile.
- Commit to one disposition per question, as engineering requests usually ask.
- Name the cause, not only the symptom: when something fails or is non-conforming, state why (which input, assumption,
  revision or condition) and what has to change.

## Scope, states and length
- Keep a scope ledger: what the request asks, what it excludes, what is under someone else's review. Items under separate
  review are mentioned, not decided; items that bear on the answer stay in even if raised elsewhere.
- Check the answer in every operating state or stage the request covers (before / during / after an event, normal and
  abnormal), not only the steady case.
- Length and precision follow the reader: a decision memo is usually 1-3 pages plus attachments; report numbers to the
  precision of the data (not six decimals); match tone and distribution to an internal or external recipient.

## Quality rules
- Be specific: dates, amounts, ratings, section numbers, document titles. No vague hedging.
- Distinguish facts from the record, requirements, and your engineering judgement.
- Check arithmetic and dates (business days, notice periods, expiry dates) with a script.
- Do not contradict yourself between the answer and the open items.
- Claim only actions that were actually taken (a request "has been sent" only if you sent it, with its record);
  otherwise write what should be done and by whom. Each follow-up becomes its own tracked item (ticket, task,
  register line with owner and date), not only a sentence inside a closed record.
- External letters carry no internal matters (internal case numbers, staff deliberations, other customers'
  correspondence, internal directives); keep those in the internal memo.
- Before netting a figure against a published baseline (capacity, budget, allowance), check what that baseline
  already includes and excludes, and say so.

## Producing the file
- Write DOCX with python-docx when available (`import docx`); otherwise use the word processing MCP tool if the task
  provides one, or build the file with LibreOffice (`soffice --headless --convert-to docx file.md` or `.html`).
- Use real headings and tables, not Markdown symbols inside the Word text.
- Save exactly at the path and file name the request gives; re-open the file to confirm it reads back, and run
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <path>`.
- If the request also asks for actions in project applications (tickets, work packages, emails, calendar), do them
  too, and make their content consistent with the memo (see the workplace-apps skill).
- End with a final message that states the answer and lists every file and record you created.

Use for any task that asks for calculations, a design, a plan, a schedule, a register or a structured submission.

# Engineering deliverables

## 1. Know exactly what is graded
- Copy every deliverable requirement from the instruction into `/tmp/ahpele/checklist.md`: path, file name, format,
  required columns/keys/tokens (exact spelling), units, row granularity ("one row per X and Y"), and any scoring rule.
- The instruction is a data contract. Use its column names, token vocabularies and IDs verbatim. Extra columns are
  usually harmless; missing or renamed ones are not.
- If the instruction states how the work is scored (e.g. hard constraints gate the score, cost objective, recall of a
  register), let that decide where effort goes: never trade a hard constraint for objective value.

## 2. Document precedence and status
- Read the governing specification first: it usually lists which standards, revisions and documents apply.
- Typical precedence (unless the project documents say otherwise): addenda / RFI responses / site instructions issued
  later > specification > drawings > schedules > vendor data > reference standards. Later dated responses override
  earlier ones on the same point.
- A document marked superseded, cancelled, withdrawn, void or draft, or an older revision of a document that exists in
  a newer revision, is not an authority. Do not cite it, do not take values from it. Record in your narrative that you
  saw it and why you set it aside.
- Words like "cancelled" inside a document's text often describe another document. Check before discarding.

## 3. Requirements table and register
- Before designing, list every hard requirement with: id, document, clause/table, requirement, limit value, unit, what
  it binds (which items). Save as `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv`.
- Hard requirements include: safety and code limits, permit/authorisation limits (discharge, noise, setbacks),
  capacities (power, flow, head, load), resource caps (equipment, crews, water, budget), milestones and deadlines.
- If a register is a deliverable, build it from this table. Cite real project documents and clauses, not the brief.
  Cite only documents that are in force.

## 4. Calculations
- Work in one unit system internally; convert at the boundary. Keep inputs, intermediate results and units in a script
  (`/tmp/ahpele/calc.py`) so numbers can be recomputed after every change.
- Take every input from a document you can cite; write assumptions down where the documents leave a choice.
- Cross-check: totals equal sums of parts, the same quantity has the same value in every file, schedules respect
  durations and predecessors, quantities respect the caps.

## 5. Build early, then improve
- Produce a complete first version of every deliverable early with conservative choices that satisfy all hard
  requirements, even if it is not optimal. An incomplete or missing file scores nothing.
- Never write placeholders (TBD, NaN, "to be determined") in a numeric field. If a value is genuinely not applicable,
  use the not-applicable convention the instruction allows (often blank, N/A or NONE).

## 6. Verify with code
- Write `/tmp/ahpele/check.py` that loads your deliverable files exactly as written and tests every requirement row and
  every checklist item (columns, tokens, units, ranges, cross-file consistency). Run it after every change.
- Run the format checker: `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <deliverable paths>`.
- For CAD/BIM outputs, re-open the file with the standard library you wrote it with and check the entities, property
  sets and attributes the instruction names.
- IFC written by hand (no BIM library): generate it with a small script, not by typing STEP lines. Copy each entity
  pattern from the example file the task provides (or from the schema), keep every attribute in order (use `$` for an
  unset one; an IfcBuildingStorey has 10 attributes, an IfcPropertySet 5, an IfcRelDefinesByProperties 6), write every REAL
  with a decimal point (`20.` or `20.0`, never `20` and never `4.5.`; coordinates, directions, depths, elevations), and double apostrophes inside strings. Run

  entity can make the whole file unreadable.

  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_clash.py <file.ifc> --point <entry x,y,z>` re-reads it with ifcopenshell's geometry
  engine in world coordinates and lists clashing pairs, element classes stacked at one spot, broken runs and the
  distance from each run to the entry point. Coordinates in `IfcCartesianPoint` are in the project length unit (a
  millimetre project takes millimetres); library helpers such as `ifcopenshell.api` placement calls take SI metres and

P: The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
P: 2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
P: The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
P: For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
P: The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
P: 3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
P: Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
P: The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
P: No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
P: 4. Interim Netted Figure
P: Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
P: Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
P: This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
P: The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
P: It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
P: It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
P: The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
P: 5. Recommendation
P: Distribution Planning recommends the following:
P: Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
P: A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")

Our reference: DER-PA-2025-ALN108-01
Dear Mr. Ashford:
Thank you for your pre-application request dated July 2, 2025 for a 3 MW pure-generation photovoltaic project on Feeder ALN-108 in the Elderpine substation service area. This letter responds to each of the three items in your request and states the capacity figure the DER Program Office will apply as of July 14, 2025.
Determination
The 3.0 MW published availability on Feeder ALN-108 is not current, and the DER Program Office cannot confirm 3.0 MW for the Elderpine Solar I project. As of July 14, 2025, the available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a new pure-generation interconnection is 0.8 MW. The requested 3.0 MW nameplate AC exceeds the available capacity by 2.2 MW.
1.  Available capacity on Feeder ALN-108
The current figure is 0.8 MW. It is derived from the published map value by applying the adjustment method stated in the map itself and the later planning update, as follows:
The 3.0 MW is the published value of record for the map, not a current statement of headroom. HCM-2024-Q2 states that published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date and that a pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication. The map has not been republished since May 15, 2024, and no later full feeder study has been issued.
Distribution Planning’s October 15, 2024 interim update netted the first post-publication entry, PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, queued September 18, 2024), producing the 1.8 MW interim figure. That update states that any queue addition after October 15, 2024 requires reassessment. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, queued February 6, 2025) in technical screening on Feeder ALN-108. No ALN-108 application appears on the July 14, 2025 On-Hold Queue Report, and no ALN-108 notice or withdrawal appears in the Withdrawal Notice Log. The further adjustment is therefore 1.8 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW.
Two earlier ALN-108 entries — PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued November 20, 2023) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued April 3, 2024) — pre-date the May 15, 2024 publication. They are outside the map’s post-publication adjustment and are not deducted a second time. The 0.8 MW is a point-in-time, straight-line netting; it is not a reservation and not a substitute for a full feeder study. A later withdrawal or change of any queued project would change the figure, and a full re-study could produce a different value after updated load, existing-DER accounting and protection screens.
2.  Conditions, restrictions and upgrade indications
No project-specific Distribution Planning study has been performed for the Elderpine Solar I project, so no project-specific upgrade scope or cost can be confirmed at this time. A 3 MW AC project is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 3-1, and would require initial screening and a system impact study. That study would determine the thermal, voltage, short-circuit and protection impacts and any network upgrades required. For classification, the governing figure is the 3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling under DIS-01 §3.1; the 3.9 MW DC array is not the interconnection capacity. The present record does not establish that 3 MW can be accommodated on Feeder ALN-108; the current available capacity is 0.8 MW.
Any formal application would take its queue position only when the application is determined complete, under Tariff §12.3, and would be processed in queue order under Tariff §12.7. The existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, system impact study) and PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), are ahead of a new filing. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a queue position.
For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply: a dedicated protection relay and a utility-owned POI recloser. A utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry is required under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, and live telemetry to the System Operations Center is a condition of permission to operate. These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.
Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.
3.  Pre-application dialogue meeting
We will hold a pre-application dialogue meeting on Tuesday, July 29, 2025, from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m. Central time, at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, or by video conference if you prefer. June Halloway (Distribution Planning) and Meera Vellanki (Manager, Interconnection Studies) will attend for Alleniom. Please confirm by July 22, 2025 and send the single-line diagram, inverter specifications, site plan and target in-service date three business days before the meeting. If July 29 does not work, we will offer August 5, 2025 at the same time. The meeting will cover the capacity record, the sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.
Map maintenance. Because HCM-2024-Q2 is more than a year old and two post-publication queue entries now affect Feeder ALN-108, Distribution Planning will place ALN-108 on the priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh under the map’s refresh criteria. The published 3.0 MW remains the map value of record until the map is republished; it should not be used for project sizing in the interim. The 0.8 MW figure in this letter is the current figure for that purpose.
We recognize that 0.8 MW is materially below the 3.0 MW you used for initial scoping. The record supports the lower figure, and we are prepared to discuss the options at the meeting.
Please direct any questions to me at (612) 555-0105 or june.halloway@alleniom.com.
Sincerely,
June Halloway

Classification: Engineering Standard — Distribution Protection
Approved by: Manager, Standards Engineering
1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.


--- page 2 ---

•
Alleniom Utilities TCS-02 — Telemetry & Communications Standard.
•
Alleniom Utilities ERP-9 — Engineering Referral Procedure.
4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.


--- page 3 ---
DPS-07 Rev 2  |  Distribution Protection Standard  |  Effective 09/15/2023
Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the


--- page 4 ---

Page 4
affected feeder warrants such a change. The determination shall be made per site by Distribution Protection
5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.
End of DPS-07 Rev 2 — Distribution Protection Standard. Distribution: Alleniom Standards Engineering master file;
Distribution Protection Engineering; Distribution Operations; DER Program Office; APUC filing (informational).

11 'Normal' Our reference: DER-PA-2025-ALN108-01
12 'Normal' Dear Mr. Ashford:
13 'Normal' Thank you for your pre-application request dated July 2, 2025 for a 3 MW pure-generation photovoltaic project on Feeder ALN-108 in the Elderpine substation service area. This letter responds to each of the three items in your request and states the capacity figure the DER Program Office will apply as of July 14, 2025.
14 'Heading 1' Determination
15 'Normal' The 3.0 MW published availability on Feeder ALN-108 is not current, and the DER Program Office cannot confirm 3.0 MW for the Elderpine Solar I project. As of July 14, 2025, the available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a new pure-generation interconnection is 0.8 MW. The requested 3.0 MW nameplate AC exceeds the available capacity by 2.2 MW.
16 'Heading 1' 1.  Available capacity on Feeder ALN-108
17 'Normal' The current figure is 0.8 MW. It is derived from the published map value by applying the adjustment method stated in the map itself and the later planning update, as follows:
18 'Normal' The 3.0 MW figure is the published value of record for the map, not a current statement of headroom. HCM-2024-Q2 states that published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date and that a pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication. The map has not been republished since May 15, 2024, and no later full feeder study has been issued.
19 'Normal' Distribution Planning’s October 15, 2024 interim update netted the first post-publication entry, PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, queued September 18, 2024), producing the 1.8 MW interim figure. That update states that any queue addition after October 15, 2024 requires reassessment. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, queued February 6, 2025) in technical screening on Feeder ALN-108; it is the only ALN-108 entry added after the October 15, 2024 update. No ALN-108 application appears on the July 14, 2025 On-Hold Queue Report, and no ALN-108 notice appears in the Withdrawal Notice Log. The further adjustment is therefore 1.8 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW.
20 'Normal' Two earlier ALN-108 entries — PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued November 20, 2023) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued April 3, 2024) — pre-date the May 15, 2024 publication. They are outside the map’s post-publication adjustment and are not deducted a second time. The 0.8 MW is a point-in-time, straight-line netting; it is not a reservation and not a substitute for a full feeder study. A later withdrawal or change of any queued project would change the figure, and a full re-study could produce a different value after updated load, existing-DER accounting and protection screens.
21 'Heading 1' 2.  Conditions, restrictions and upgrade indications
22 'Normal' No project-specific Distribution Planning study has been performed for the Elderpine Solar I project, so no project-specific upgrade scope or cost can be confirmed at this time. A 3 MW AC project is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 3-1, and would require initial screening and a system impact study. That study would determine the thermal, voltage, short-circuit and protection impacts and any network upgrades required. For classification, the governing figure is the 3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling under DIS-01 §3.1; the 3.9 MW DC array is not the interconnection capacity. A lower export limit would be recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 Power Control System certification and an approved Control Narrative under DIS-01 §3.6; no such submissions accompanied the pre-application, so the 3 MW nameplate governs.
23 'Normal' Any formal application would take its queue position only when the application is determined complete, under Tariff §12.3, and would be processed in queue order under Tariff §12.7. The existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, system impact study) and PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), are ahead of a new filing. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a queue position.
24 'Normal' For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply: a dedicated protection relay and a utility-owned POI recloser. A utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry is required under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, and live telemetry to the System Operations Center is a condition of permission to operate. These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.
25 'Normal' Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.
26 'Heading 1' 3.  Pre-application dialogue meeting
27 'Normal' We will hold a pre-application dialogue meeting on Tuesday, July 29, 2025, from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m. Central time, at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, or by video conference if you prefer. June Halloway (Distribution Planning) and Meera Vellanki (Manager, Interconnection Studies) will attend for Alleniom. Please confirm by July 22, 2025 and send the single-line diagram, inverter specifications, site plan and target in-service date three business days before the meeting. If July 29 does not work, we will offer August 5, 2025 at the same time. The meeting will cover the capacity record, the sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.
28 'Normal' Map maintenance. Because HCM-2024-Q2 is more than a year old and two post-publication queue entries now affect Feeder ALN-108, Distribution Planning will place ALN-108 on the priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh under the map’s refresh criteria. The published 3.0 MW remains the map value of record until the map is republished; it should not be used for project sizing in the interim. The 0.8 MW figure in this letter is the current figure for that purpose.
29 'Normal' We recognize that 0.8 MW is materially below the 3.0 MW you used for initial scoping. The record supports the lower figure, and we are prepared to discuss the options at the meeting.
30 'Normal' Please direct any questions to me at (612) 555-0105 or june.halloway@alleniom.com.

Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com

1. Purpose
This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
Attribute | Value
Feeder ID | ALN-108
Substation | Elderpine
Nominal voltage | 13.2 kV
DER category | Pure Generation
Last completed planning study | 04/2024
Published available capacity | 3.0 MW
Publication date | 05/15/2024


The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
Queue date | Feeder | Requested capacity (nameplate) | DER category
09/18/2024 | ALN-108 | 1.2 MW | Pure Generation


The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
4. Interim Netted Figure
Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
5. Recommendation
Distribution Planning recommends the following:
Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.
