checks={
 'REQ-001': lambda: abs(res['current_available_mw']-(res['published_mw']-res['post_publication_mw']))<1e-9 and 'adjusted for queue entries' in low,
 'REQ-002': lambda: abs(res['published_mw']-3.0)<1e-9 and '3.0 MW' in text,
 'REQ-003': lambda: ('republished' in low or 'value of record' in low) and 'map refresh' in low,
 'REQ-004': lambda: 'priority list' in low and 'refresh criteria' in low,
 'REQ-005': lambda: abs(ids['PXA-2024-0231']['capacity_mw']-1.2)<1e-9 and ids['PXA-2024-0231']['queue_date']=='2024-09-18' and 'September 18, 2024' in text,
 'REQ-006': lambda: abs(res['plan']['interim_mw']-1.8)<1e-9 and '1.8 MW' in text,
 'REQ-007': lambda: 'October 15, 2024' in text and 'reassess' in low and 'point-in-time' in low,
 'REQ-008': lambda: 'Distribution Planning' in text and '0.8 MW' in text,
 'REQ-009': lambda: feeders=={'ALN-108'},
 'REQ-010': lambda: 'Tariff §12.3' in text and 'complete' in low and 'queue position' in low,
 'REQ-011': lambda: 'Tariff §12.7' in text and 'queue order' in low,
 'REQ-012': lambda: '3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling' in text and '3.9 MW DC' in text,
 'REQ-013': lambda: 'medium-scale' in low and 'system impact study' in low and '3 MW' in text,
 'REQ-014': lambda: 'commercial small-scale' in low and '500 kW to 1 MW' in text and 'SRP-3' in text,
 'REQ-015': lambda: 'Category 3' in text and 'dedicated protection relay' in low and 'POI recloser' in text,

 'REQ-018': lambda: 'TCS-02 §5' in text and 'utility-owned RTU' in text and 'live telemetry' in low,

 'REQ-020': lambda: '12 complete months of AMI interval data' in text,
 'REQ-021': lambda: 'feeder penetration' in low and 'screens' in low,
 'REQ-022': lambda: 'short-circuit' in low and 'screens' in low,
 'REQ-023': lambda: 'priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh' in low and 'refresh criteria' in low,
 'REQ-024': lambda: all(x in text for x in ['HCM-2024-Q2','PLN-ALN-108-2024-10','Tariff §12.3','DIS-01 Rev 4']),
 'REQ-025': lambda: all(x in text for x in ['HCM-2024-Q2','PLN-ALN-108-2024-10','Tariff §12.7','DIS-01 Rev 4']),
 'REQ-026': lambda: 'Tariff §12.7' in text and 'DIS-01 Rev 4' in text,

 'REQ-028': lambda: 'UL 1741' in text and 'Control Narrative' in text and '§3.6' in text,
 'REQ-029': lambda: 'utility-owned POI recloser' in text,
}
ok(set(checks)=={r['Req_ID'] for r in reqs}, 'requirements.csv IDs do not match check mapping')
for r in reqs:
    rid=r['Req_ID']
    try:
        val=checks[rid]()
    except Exception as e:
        val=False
        print(f'ERROR checking {rid}: {e}')
    ok(val, f'failed requirement {rid}: {r["Requirement"][:120]}')

util_req=3.0/0.8
util_option=0.8/0.8
print(f'Capacity limit: current available = {res["current_available_mw"]:.1f} MW')
print(f'Worst case utilisation: requested 3.0 MW / 0.8 MW = {util_req:.2f} ({util_req*100:.0f}%) -> exceeds limit by {res["excess_mw"]:.1f} MW')
print(f'At-size option: 0.8 MW / 0.8 MW = {util_option:.2f} (100%) -> no margin at the limit; recommend sizing below 0.8 MW')
ok(util_req>1.0, 'request does not exceed available capacity as expected')

ok(case['case']['status']=='Closed', 'WP44 is not Closed')
ok(case['case']['done_ratio']==100, 'WP44 done ratio is not 100')

for w in case['followups']:

ok(case['calendar_event']['end']=='2025-07-29T11:00:00-05:00', 'calendar hold end wrong')

that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


--- page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.


--- page 3 ---
§4 TIMELINES
Timelines below run from the date on which Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11
to Distribution Protection Engineering. Business days exclude weekends and federal holidays.

Where the reviewer requests reclassification, the request is decided in writing within two business days.
Extensions to the timelines above are permitted only in writing, are issued by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and are copied to the DER Program Manager and Regulatory Affairs. Applications
shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.
§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.
The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.
Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.

# Independent review — ALN-108 pre-application response

Reviewer basis: request dated 07/02/2025; record as of 07/14/2025; deliverable `/filesystem/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` and filed copy `/DER_Program/Correspondence/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx`. I did not rely on the author's `check.py`/`calc.py` results; I re-read the source files and re-computed the capacity record.

## Findings (most serious first)

1. **MAJOR — The 0.8 MW sizing path omits mandatory protection and telemetry requirements for that path, and the standards conflict is not routed under ERP-9.**  
   - **Requirement:** DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2: “Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.” DPS-07 §2 includes commercial small-scale DER (500 kW–1 MW) and any DER capable of exporting. TCS-02 Rev 1 §5: “≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry,” and TCS-02 §2 applies to commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW. DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 says Category 2 “POI recloser: not required,” which conflicts with DPS-07 §4.2; DIS-01 §8 requires such conflicts to be referred per-site under ERP-9 §3, and ERP-9 §3 says no “winning” document is selected across the program.  
   - **What the deliverable has:** Section 2, p.3, says the project “can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class … with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3 …,” but it mentions neither the DPS-07 §4.2 POI recloser nor the TCS-02 §5 RTU/SCADA/live-telemetry condition for that option. The only POI-recloser and RTU statements are in the preceding paragraph addressed to “a 3 MW pure-generation site.”  
   - **What it should be:** State that the 0.8 MW option is still an in-scope export-capable site: DPS-07 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser and TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before PTO, notwithstanding DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2; identify the DIS-01/DPS-07 conflict and say it will be resolved by a per-site ERP-9 Form ER-11 determination, not by selecting one standard. The equipment lead time in the 06/30/2025 Supplier Lead-Time Report is ~8 months for both RTU and POI recloser, so this also affects the customer’s Q4 2026 target.  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Standards/DPS-07_Rev2_Distribution_Protection_Standard.pdf` pp.1–3 §2, §4.2; `/filesystem/Standards/TCS-02_Telemetry_Comms_Standard.pdf` pp.1–4 §2, §5; `/filesystem/Standards/DIS-01_Rev4_DER_Interconnection_Standard.pdf` p.5 Table 5-1, p.7 §8; `/filesystem/Standards/ERP-9_Engineering_Referral_Procedure.pdf` pp.2–3 §3; `/filesystem/Equipment/2025-06_Supplier_Lead_Time_Report.xlsx` Summary/Orders on Hand. The author’s own `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv` REQ-018 and REQ-029 say these requirements apply to “3 MW project and 0.8 MW option,” but the letter’s 0.8 paragraph does not carry them.

2. **MAJOR — The answer to request item 2 lists only two of the Category 3 requirements; the required DER-side disconnect, DER breaker/protection scheme, anti-islanding/transfer-trip provision and metering are omitted.**  
   - **Requirement:** DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1, Category 3 (1 MW–5 MW export sites): DER-side disconnect “Required (customer-owned lockable visible-break)”; dedicated protection relay required; DER breaker with protection relay scheme “As specified per site by protection engineering”; POI recloser required; anti-islanding “Dedicated relay scheme with transfer trip where required by protection engineering”; metering “Bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as feeder configuration requires”; utility RTU/SCADA telemetry required.  
   - **What the deliverable has:** p.3: “For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply: a dedicated protection relay and a utility-owned POI recloser. A utility-owned RTU … is required ….” The colon reads as an exhaustive list; the DER-side disconnect, DER breaker scheme, anti-islanding/transfer trip and metering are absent.  
   - **What it should be:** Say “including, at minimum” and list the omitted Category 3 items, or state that the full Table 5-1 Category 3 set applies and identify the items requiring site-specific protection engineering. The request expressly asks for “known conditions, restrictions, or upgrade indications”; this is a direct content gap.  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Standards/DIS-01_Rev4_DER_Interconnection_Standard.pdf` p.5 Table 5-1; deliverable p.3.

3. **MAJOR — The 0.8 MW figure rests on an unstated assumption that the two pre-publication ALN-108 queue entries were already in the 3.0 MW baseline; the cited record does not establish that.**  
   - **Requirement/clause cited:** HCM-2024-Q2 Title Block “Basis”: the published value is a “Feeder-level planning study using recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study….” The HCM “Applicability” says published values do not reflect queue activity recorded after publication and a pre-application response is prepared against the published value “as adjusted for queue entries added since publication.” The letter uses the latter method and says PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued 11/20/2023) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued 04/03/2024) are “not deducted a second time.”  
   - **What the deliverable has:** p.2: “Two earlier ALN-108 entries … pre-date the May 15, 2024 publication. They are outside the map’s post-publication adjustment and are not deducted a second time.”  
   - **What the record shows:** The 07/14/2025 Existing-DER Register Extract’s scope is “In-service or previously in-service DER sites,” and it does not list either PXA-2023-0894 or PXA-2024-0091. The 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report shows PXA-2023-0894 as “ISA executed” and PXA-2024-0091 as “construction,” not in service. The 10/15/2024 planning study §3 identifies only the 1.2 MW post-publication entry and does not state that the two pre-publication entries were included in the 3.0 MW baseline. The HCM basis speaks of “existing interconnected DER,” not queued/ISA-executed projects.  
   - **Why it matters:** If the 3.0 MW baseline did not include those 1.79 MW of pre-publication queued capacity, the current headroom is 3.0 − 1.1 − 0.69 − 1.2 − 1.0 = **−0.99 MW** (no headroom), not 0.8 MW, and the 3.0 MW request exceeds available capacity by 3.99 MW, not 2.2 MW. The letter must either cite the 04/2024 study/queue snapshot that included the two entries or deduct them; as written, the central 0.8 MW determination is not supported on the face of the cited record.  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Planning/Hosting_Capacity_Map_Export_2024-05-15.xlsx` Title Block “Basis”/“Applicability”; `/filesystem/Planning/2024-10-15_ALN-108_Planning_Study.docx` §§2–4; `/filesystem/Screening/Existing_DER_Register_Extract.xlsx` Register/Notes; `/filesystem/Queue/2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx` ALN-108 rows; deliverable p.2.

4. **MINOR — “The map has not been republished since May 15, 2024” is stronger than the record proves.**  
   - **Requirement/record:** HCM-2024-Q2 Title Block commits to a “Quarterly refresh” and says the map “is republished on a quarterly cadence.” The document store `/DER_Program/Planning` contains only the 05/15/2024 HCM export; no later edition is in the record. The letter’s statement is a factual claim about publication history, not merely about the record before the reviewer.  
   - **What it should be:** “No later edition of the map is in the record as of 07/14/2025” (or cite the publication history). This is a wording/precision issue, not a change to the 0.8 calculation.  
   - **Evidence:** HCM Title Block “Refresh commitment”; `/DER_Program/Planning` file list (three files, HCM dated 2024-05-15 only); deliverable p.2.

5. **MINOR — PXA-2024-0231 is reported as “system impact study” in the Active Queue Report, but the 07/14/2025 SIS Backlog Status has no row for it.**  
   - **Requirement/record:** The letter cites PXA-2024-0231 as “1.2 MW, system impact study” (p.3) and uses its 1.2 MW in the capacity table. The 07/14/2025 SIS Backlog Status (DPG-SIS-BL-2025-07 Rev 1) lists 44 studies and does not contain PXA-2024-0231.  
   - **Effect:** The capacity treatment is unaffected because the 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report still carries the project as an active ALN-108 queue entry and the 10/15/2024 planning study netted its 1.2 MW. But the study-status statement is not corroborated by the companion SIS record; the case file should note the inconsistency and verify the status with the DER Planning Group (the author’s own review noted this as a “non-material discrepancy”).  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Queue/2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx` row PXA-2024-0231; `/filesystem/Studies/SIS_Backlog_Status_2025-07.xlsx` SIS Backlog rows; deliverable p.3.

6. **MINOR — The priority-refresh action is only a follow-up due 08/18/2025, after the 07/14/2025 external communication, while RA-2025-07-01 §3.7 asks for a priority refresh request before communicating a map capacity figure.**  
   - **Requirement:** RA-2025-07-01 §3.7: “Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.”  
   - **What the deliverable/case has:** The letter dated 07/14/2025 says Distribution Planning “will place ALN-108 on the priority list”; the only recorded priority-refresh action is WP47, created as a follow-up, due 08/18/2025. No prior request/record of priority listing is in the case file before the letter.  
   - **What it should be:** Either document that the priority-refresh request was made before the 07/14/2025 letter, or add the request to the record and note the sequencing. If §3.7’s “before” is read only as applying to the confirmation step, this is a documentation gap rather than a substantive violation; I record it as MINOR for that reason.  
   - **Evidence:** `/tmp/ahpele/case_state.json` WP47 due 08/18/2025; OpenProject WP47 description; deliverable p.3; `/filesystem/Correspondence/2025-07-01_RegAffairs_Tasking_Memo.docx` §3.7.

## Checks that passed

- **Capacity arithmetic (on the letter’s stated method):** HCM ALN-108 published 3.0 MW; post-publication queue entries PXA-2024-0231 1.2 MW (queued 09/18/2024) and PXA-2025-0044 1.0 MW (queued 02/06/2025); 3.0 − 1.2 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW; 3.0 − 0.8 = 2.2 MW. The letter states all three values and the arithmetic in Table 1. I verified the four ALN-108 rows in the 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report: PXA-2023-0894 1.1 MW (11/20/2023), PXA-2024-0091 690 kW (04/03/2024), PXA-2024-0231 1.2 MW (09/18/2024), PXA-2025-0044 1.0 MW (02/06/2025).
- **No ALN-108 on-hold or withdrawal record:** Searches of the 07/14/2025 On-Hold Queue Report (141 hold rows) and Withdrawal Notice Log found no ALN-108 entry; the letter’s statement is correct.
- **Classification and review path:** 3.0 MW AC is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 3-1 (1–5 MW) and requires initial screening plus a system impact study; 0.8 MW is commercial small-scale (500 kW–1 MW) and requires initial screening plus supplemental review under SRP-3. The letter states this correctly.
- **Controlled-capacity:** No UL 1741/UL 3141 PCS certification or approved Control Narrative accompanied the request; DIS-01 §3.6 therefore makes nameplate (3.0 MW AC) the classification basis. The letter states this correctly. The 3.9 MW DC figure is not the interconnection capacity under DIS-01 §3.1.
- **Queue process:** Tariff §12.3 (queue position on completeness) and §12.7 (queue-order processing) are correctly cited; a pre-application does not reserve capacity or queue position. The letter says so.
- **Format and filing:** `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py /filesystem/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` reports “no problems found”; the file is a valid DOCX, 41,619 bytes, renders to 3 pages, and the `/DER_Program/Correspondence/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` copy is present at the same size. The letter is dated 07/14/2025, after the 07/02/2025 request and before the 08/15/2025 League response.
- **Case tracking:** OpenProject WP44 is Closed, 100%, due 08/15/2025; its description records the 0.8 MW call and the follow-up WPs. WP47 (priority refresh/re-study, due 08/18/2025), WP48 (formal application tracking, due 08/18/2025) and WP49 (07/29/2025 meeting, due 07/29/2025) exist; the 07/29/2025 calendar event exists. The case call and the letter agree on 0.8 MW / 2.2 MW shortfall.
- **Requirement scan:** `ahpele_reqscan.py --check` reports 68/68 strong candidates reviewed, 0 unreviewed; `--register` reports 29 rows, 0 notfound/unmatched/multi. The scan does not validate engineering correctness; findings 1–5 above are outside its checks.

## Bottom line

The letter’s central arithmetic and refusal to confirm 3.0 MW are correct on the record’s post-publication netting method, and the required DOCX/case-tracking/deliverable formalities are in place. The material technical gaps are (i) the 0.8 MW option is presented without the mandatory DPS-07 §4.2 POI recloser and TCS-02 §5 RTU/live-telemetry conditions (and without the required ERP-9 routing of the DIS-01/DPS-07 conflict), (ii) the 3 MW “Category 3 requirements” list is incomplete, and (iii) the 0.8 MW figure assumes, without citing, that the two pre-publication ALN-108 queue entries were already in the 3.0 MW baseline; if they were not, the correct headroom is negative, not 0.8 MW.

# Independent review — ALN-108 pre-application response

Reviewer basis: request dated 07/02/2025; record as of 07/14/2025; deliverable `/filesystem/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` and filed copy `/DER_Program/Correspondence/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx`. I did not rely on the author's `check.py`/`calc.py` results; I re-read the source files and re-computed the capacity record.

No BLOCKING format or missing-deliverable defect was found. The material findings are MAJOR content/engineering gaps (items 1–2); items 3–6 are MINOR documentation/precision issues.

## Findings (most serious first)

1. **MAJOR — The 0.8 MW sizing path omits mandatory protection and telemetry requirements for that path, and the standards conflict is not routed under ERP-9.**  
   - **Requirement:** DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2: “Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection (POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.” DPS-07 §2 includes commercial small-scale DER (500 kW–1 MW) and any DER capable of exporting. TCS-02 Rev 1 §5: “≥500 kW requires utility-owned RTU + SCADA telemetry; no PTO without live telemetry,” and TCS-02 §2 applies to commercial small-scale 500 kW–1 MW. DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1 says Category 2 “POI recloser: not required,” which conflicts with DPS-07 §4.2; DIS-01 §8 requires such conflicts to be referred per-site under ERP-9 §3, and ERP-9 §3 says no “winning” document is selected across the program.  
   - **What the deliverable has:** Section 2, p.3, says the project “can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class … with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3 …,” but it mentions neither the DPS-07 §4.2 POI recloser nor the TCS-02 §5 RTU/SCADA/live-telemetry condition for that option. The only POI-recloser and RTU statements are in the preceding paragraph addressed to “a 3 MW pure-generation site.”  
   - **What it should be:** State that the 0.8 MW option is still an in-scope export-capable site: DPS-07 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser and TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before PTO, notwithstanding DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2; the customer-owned lockable visible-break DER-side disconnect is also required under DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2. Identify the DIS-01/DPS-07 conflict and say it will be resolved by a per-site ERP-9 Form ER-11 determination, not by selecting one standard. The equipment lead time in the 06/30/2025 Supplier Lead-Time Report is ~8 months for both RTU and POI recloser, so this also affects the customer’s Q4 2026 target.  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Standards/DPS-07_Rev2_Distribution_Protection_Standard.pdf` pp.1–3 §2, §4.2; `/filesystem/Standards/TCS-02_Telemetry_Comms_Standard.pdf` pp.1–4 §2, §5; `/filesystem/Standards/DIS-01_Rev4_DER_Interconnection_Standard.pdf` p.5 Table 5-1, p.7 §8; `/filesystem/Standards/ERP-9_Engineering_Referral_Procedure.pdf` pp.2–3 §3; `/filesystem/Equipment/2025-06_Supplier_Lead_Time_Report.xlsx` Summary/Orders on Hand. The author’s own `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv` REQ-018 and REQ-029 say these requirements apply to “3 MW project and 0.8 MW option,” but the letter’s 0.8 paragraph does not carry them. The same register contains REQ-016 (“Category 2 … does not require a POI recloser”), which contradicts REQ-029 and DPS-07 §4.2; the author’s `check.py` test for REQ-016 only looks for “commercial small-scale” and “0.8 MW,” so it does not catch the conflict.

2. **MAJOR — The answer to request item 2 lists only two of the Category 3 requirements; the required DER-side disconnect, DER breaker/protection scheme, anti-islanding/transfer-trip provision and metering are omitted.**  
   - **Requirement:** DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 5-1, Category 3 (1 MW–5 MW export sites): DER-side disconnect “Required (customer-owned lockable visible-break)”; dedicated protection relay required; DER breaker with protection relay scheme “As specified per site by protection engineering”; POI recloser required; anti-islanding “Dedicated relay scheme with transfer trip where required by protection engineering”; metering “Bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as feeder configuration requires”; utility RTU/SCADA telemetry required.  
   - **What the deliverable has:** p.3: “For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply: a dedicated protection relay and a utility-owned POI recloser. A utility-owned RTU … is required ….” The colon reads as an exhaustive list; the DER-side disconnect, DER breaker scheme, anti-islanding/transfer trip and metering are absent.  
   - **What it should be:** Say “including, at minimum” and list the omitted Category 3 items, or state that the full Table 5-1 Category 3 set applies and identify the items requiring site-specific protection engineering. The request expressly asks for “known conditions, restrictions, or upgrade indications”; this is a direct content gap.  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Standards/DIS-01_Rev4_DER_Interconnection_Standard.pdf` p.5 Table 5-1; deliverable p.3.

3. **MINOR — The letter’s explanation for excluding the two pre-publication ALN-108 queue entries is conclusory; it should quote the map’s post-publication adjustment clause.**  
   - **Requirement/clause cited:** HCM-2024-Q2 “Applicability”: “Published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date … A pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication.” The letter says PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued 11/20/2023) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued 04/03/2024) “pre-date the May 15, 2024 publication. They are outside the map’s post-publication adjustment and are not deducted a second time.”  
   - **What the record shows:** The published 3.0 MW is the baseline “as of the publication date”; the HCM applicability limits the adjustment to queue entries added after publication, which supports treating the two pre-publication entries as part of the published baseline. The letter’s “not deducted a second time” is an inference from that clause but does not quote it or state that the 04/2024 study/queue snapshot included the two entries. The Existing-DER Register Extract (in-service/previously in-service sites) does not list either project, and the Active Queue Report shows them as “ISA executed” and “construction,” so a reader could otherwise ask whether they were counted at all.  
   - **What it should be:** Quote the HCM “as adjusted for queue entries added since publication” clause and state expressly that the published 3.0 MW baseline already reflects the pre-publication queue record; this is a citation/documentation improvement, not a change to the 0.8 MW arithmetic on the map’s stated method.  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Planning/Hosting_Capacity_Map_Export_2024-05-15.xlsx` Title Block “Basis”/“Applicability”; `/filesystem/Planning/2024-10-15_ALN-108_Planning_Study.docx` §§2–4; `/filesystem/Screening/Existing_DER_Register_Extract.xlsx` Register/Notes; `/filesystem/Queue/2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx` ALN-108 rows; deliverable p.2.

4. **MINOR — “The map has not been republished since May 15, 2024” is stronger than the record proves.**  
   - **Requirement/record:** HCM-2024-Q2 Title Block commits to a “Quarterly refresh” and says the map “is republished on a quarterly cadence.” The document store `/DER_Program/Planning` contains only the 05/15/2024 HCM export; no later edition is in the record. The letter’s statement is a factual claim about publication history, not merely about the record before the reviewer.  
   - **What it should be:** “No later edition of the map is in the record as of 07/14/2025” (or cite the publication history). This is a wording/precision issue, not a change to the 0.8 calculation.  
   - **Evidence:** HCM Title Block “Refresh commitment”; `/DER_Program/Planning` file list (three files, HCM dated 2024-05-15 only); deliverable p.2.

5. **MINOR — PXA-2024-0231 is reported as “system impact study” in the Active Queue Report, but the 07/14/2025 SIS Backlog Status has no row for it.**  
   - **Requirement/record:** The letter cites PXA-2024-0231 as “1.2 MW, system impact study” (p.3) and uses its 1.2 MW in the capacity table. The 07/14/2025 SIS Backlog Status (DPG-SIS-BL-2025-07 Rev 1) lists 44 studies and does not contain PXA-2024-0231.  
   - **Effect:** The capacity treatment is unaffected because the 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report still carries the project as an active ALN-108 queue entry and the 10/15/2024 planning study netted its 1.2 MW. But the study-status statement is not corroborated by the companion SIS record; the case file should note the inconsistency and verify the status with the DER Planning Group (the author’s own review noted this as a “non-material discrepancy”).  
   - **Evidence:** `/filesystem/Queue/2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx` row PXA-2024-0231; `/filesystem/Studies/SIS_Backlog_Status_2025-07.xlsx` SIS Backlog rows; deliverable p.3.

6. **MINOR — The priority-refresh action is only a follow-up due 08/18/2025, after the 07/14/2025 external communication, while RA-2025-07-01 §3.7 asks for a priority refresh request before communicating a map capacity figure.**  
   - **Requirement:** RA-2025-07-01 §3.7: “Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.”  
   - **What the deliverable/case has:** The letter dated 07/14/2025 says Distribution Planning “will place ALN-108 on the priority list”; the only recorded priority-refresh action is WP47, created as a follow-up, due 08/18/2025. No prior request/record of priority listing is in the case file before the letter.  
   - **What it should be:** Either document that the priority-refresh request was made before the 07/14/2025 letter, or add the request to the record and note the sequencing. If §3.7’s “before” is read only as applying to the confirmation step, this is a documentation gap rather than a substantive violation; I record it as MINOR for that reason.  
   - **Evidence:** `/tmp/ahpele/case_state.json` WP47 due 08/18/2025; OpenProject WP47 description; deliverable p.3; `/filesystem/Correspondence/2025-07-01_RegAffairs_Tasking_Memo.docx` §3.7.

## Checks that passed

- **Capacity arithmetic (on the letter’s stated method):** HCM ALN-108 published 3.0 MW; post-publication queue entries PXA-2024-0231 1.2 MW (queued 09/18/2024) and PXA-2025-0044 1.0 MW (queued 02/06/2025); 3.0 − 1.2 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW; 3.0 − 0.8 = 2.2 MW. The letter states all three values and the arithmetic in Table 1. I verified the four ALN-108 rows in the 07/14/2025 Active Queue Report: PXA-2023-0894 1.1 MW (11/20/2023), PXA-2024-0091 690 kW (04/03/2024), PXA-2024-0231 1.2 MW (09/18/2024), PXA-2025-0044 1.0 MW (02/06/2025).
- **No ALN-108 on-hold or withdrawal record:** Searches of the 07/14/2025 On-Hold Queue Report (141 hold rows) and Withdrawal Notice Log found no ALN-108 entry; the letter’s statement is correct.
- **Classification and review path:** 3.0 MW AC is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4 Table 3-1 (1–5 MW) and requires initial screening plus a system impact study; 0.8 MW is commercial small-scale (500 kW–1 MW) and requires initial screening plus supplemental review under SRP-3. The letter states this correctly.
- **Controlled-capacity:** No UL 1741/UL 3141 PCS certification or approved Control Narrative accompanied the request; DIS-01 §3.6 therefore makes nameplate (3.0 MW AC) the classification basis. The letter states this correctly. The 3.9 MW DC figure is not the interconnection capacity under DIS-01 §3.1.
- **Queue process:** Tariff §12.3 (queue position on completeness) and §12.7 (queue-order processing) are correctly cited; a pre-application does not reserve capacity or queue position. The letter says so.
- **Format and filing:** `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py /filesystem/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` reports “no problems found”; the file is a valid DOCX, 41,619 bytes, renders to 3 pages, and the `/DER_Program/Correspondence/ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx` copy is present at the same size. The letter is dated 07/14/2025, after the 07/02/2025 request and before the 08/15/2025 League response.
- **Case tracking:** OpenProject WP44 is Closed, 100%, due 08/15/2025; its description records the 0.8 MW call and the follow-up WPs. WP47 (priority refresh/re-study, due 08/18/2025), WP48 (formal application tracking, due 08/18/2025) and WP49 (07/29/2025 meeting, due 07/29/2025) exist; the 07/29/2025 calendar event exists. The case call and the letter agree on 0.8 MW / 2.2 MW shortfall.
- **Requirement scan:** `ahpele_reqscan.py --check` reports 68/68 strong candidates reviewed, 0 unreviewed; `--register` reports 29 rows, 0 notfound/unmatched/multi. The scan does not validate engineering correctness; findings 1–6 above are outside its checks.

## Bottom line

The letter’s central arithmetic and refusal to confirm 3.0 MW are correct on the record’s post-publication netting method, and the required DOCX/case-tracking/deliverable formalities are in place. The material technical gaps are (i) the 0.8 MW option is presented without the mandatory DPS-07 §4.2 POI recloser and TCS-02 §5 RTU/live-telemetry conditions (and without the required ERP-9 routing of the DIS-01/DPS-07 conflict), and (ii) the 3 MW “Category 3 requirements” list is incomplete. The remaining items are documentation/precision issues: the letter should quote the HCM clause that supports excluding pre-publication queue entries, should say “no later map edition is in the record” rather than “has not been republished,” and should note the PXA-2024-0231 SIS-status discrepancy.

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent checks of the ALN-108 pre-application response against the record and requirements.csv."""
import csv, re, sys, json, datetime
from pathlib import Path
import docx
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/ahpele')
import calc

ROOT = Path('/filesystem')
DOC = ROOT/'ALN-108_PreApplication_Response.docx'
FAIL=[]
def ok(cond,msg):
    if not cond: FAIL.append(msg)
    return cond

res = calc.compute()
texts=[]
d=docx.Document(DOC)
texts += [p.text for p in d.paragraphs]
for t in d.tables:
    for row in t.rows:
        for c in row.cells: texts.append(c.text)
raw='\n'.join(texts)
text=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',raw.replace('−','-').replace('–','-').replace('—','-'))
low=text.lower()

# ---- Core capacity arithmetic ----
ok(abs(res['published_mw']-3.0)<1e-9, 'published baseline is not 3.0 MW')
ok(abs(res['post_publication_mw']-2.2)<1e-9, 'post-publication netting is not 2.2 MW')
ok(abs(res['current_available_mw']-0.8)<1e-9, 'current available capacity is not 0.8 MW')
ok(abs(res['excess_mw']-2.2)<1e-9, '3.0 MW excess over 0.8 MW is not 2.2 MW')
ids={r['id']:r for r in res['post_publication']}
ok(set(ids)=={'PXA-2024-0231','PXA-2025-0044'}, f'post-publication ALN-108 entries wrong: {sorted(ids)}')
ok(abs(ids['PXA-2024-0231']['capacity_mw']-1.2)<1e-9, 'PXA-2024-0231 is not 1.2 MW')
ok(abs(ids['PXA-2025-0044']['capacity_mw']-1.0)<1e-9, 'PXA-2025-0044 is not 1.0 MW')
ok(ids['PXA-2024-0231']['queue_date']=='2024-09-18', 'PXA-2024-0231 queue date wrong')
ok(ids['PXA-2025-0044']['queue_date']=='2025-02-06', 'PXA-2025-0044 queue date wrong')

# ---- Document content: the call and its basis ----
must=[
 ('0.8 MW', 'current capacity 0.8 MW'),
 ('3.0 MW', 'published/requested 3.0 MW'),
 ('1.2 MW', '1.2 MW queue entry'),
 ('1.0 MW', '1.0 MW queue entry'),
 ('2.2 MW', '2.2 MW excess'),
 ('not current', 'published figure stated not current'),
 ('cannot confirm 3.0 MW', 'clear refusal to confirm 3.0 MW'),
 ('PXA-2024-0231', 'Grantwyck application ID'),
 ('PXA-2025-0044', 'Cindermere application ID'),
 ('September 18, 2024', 'Grantwyck queue date'),
 ('February 6, 2025', 'Cindermere queue date'),
 ('1.8 MW', 'interim figure'),
 ('October 15, 2024', 'planning update date'),
 ('HCM-2024-Q2', 'map document'),
 ('PLN-ALN-108-2024-10', 'planning study document'),
 ('Tariff §12.3', 'queue-position clause'),
 ('Tariff §12.7', 'queue-order clause'),
 ('DIS-01 Rev 4', 'interconnection standard'),
 ('Table 3-1', 'classification table'),
 ('Table 5-1', 'protection table'),
 ('TCS-02 §5', 'telemetry condition'),
 ('medium-scale', '3 MW class'),
 ('system impact study', '3 MW review path'),
 ('commercial small-scale', '0.8 MW class'),
 ('SRP-3', 'supplemental review'),
 ('10:00-16:00', 'daytime window'),
 ('12 complete months', 'AMI data window'),
 ('priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh', 'map maintenance follow-up'),
 ('July 29, 2025', 'meeting date'),
 ('June Halloway', 'signatory'),
 ('Distribution Planning Engineer', 'signatory title'),
 ('(612) 555-0105', 'contact phone'),
 ('june.halloway@alleniom.com', 'contact email'),
]
for token,label in must:
    ok(token.lower() in low, f'missing {label}: {token!r}')

# Three requested items present
for token in ['1. Written confirmation', '2. Known conditions', '3. Pre-application dialogue meeting']:
    ok(token.lower() in low, f'missing requested item: {token}')

# No other feeder is discussed
feeders=set(re.findall(r'ALN-\d{3}', text))
ok(feeders=={'ALN-108'}, f'other feeders cited: {sorted(feeders)}')
ok('work package' not in low and 'wp 44' not in low and 'regulatory affairs' not in low and 'directive' not in low,
   'internal case/directive material appears in external letter')
for bad in ['CEL-2024-Q4','Witness Test Waiver','POL-QM-05','Queue Management']:
    ok(bad.lower() not in low, f'superseded/irrelevant document cited: {bad}')

# Names/titles against contact directory
import openpyxl
wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(ROOT/'DER_Program_Contact_Directory.xlsx',data_only=True)
ws=wb['Contact Directory']
dirrows={}
for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=8,values_only=True):
    if row[0]: dirrows[row[0]]={'title':row[1],'phone':row[4],'email':row[3]}
ok('June Halloway' in dirrows, 'June Halloway not in contact directory')
ok(dirrows.get('June Halloway',{}).get('title')=='Distribution Planning Engineer', 'June Halloway title mismatch')
ok(dirrows.get('June Halloway',{}).get('phone')=='(612) 555-0105', 'June Halloway phone mismatch')
ok(dirrows.get('June Halloway',{}).get('email')=='june.halloway@alleniom.com', 'June Halloway email mismatch')
ok(dirrows.get('Meera Vellanki',{}).get('title')=='Manager, Interconnection Studies', 'Meera Vellanki title mismatch')

# Dates: no source/record date after 2025-07-14; action dates allowed
allowed_action={datetime.date(2025,7,22),datetime.date(2025,7,29),datetime.date(2025,8,5)}
dates=set()
for m in re.finditer(r'(January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+(\d{1,2}),\s+(\d{4})', text):
    dates.add(datetime.date(int(m.group(3)), datetime.datetime.strptime(m.group(1),'%B').month, int(m.group(2))))
for m in re.finditer(r'(\d{1,2})/(\d{1,2})/(\d{4})', text):
    dates.add(datetime.date(int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2))))
for dt in sorted(dates):
    if dt>datetime.date(2025,7,14):
        ok(dt in allowed_action, f'date after as-of date used: {dt}')
# weekday checks
ok(datetime.date(2025,7,22).weekday()==1, '07/22/2025 is not a Tuesday')
ok(datetime.date(2025,7,29).weekday()==1, '07/29/2025 is not a Tuesday')
ok(datetime.date(2025,8,5).weekday()==1, '08/05/2025 is not a Tuesday')
ok(datetime.date(2025,7,14)>=datetime.date(2025,7,2), 'response predates request')
ok(datetime.date(2025,7,14)<=datetime.date(2025,8,15), 'response misses 08/15/2025 deadline')

# ---- Requirements.csv: one check per row ----
reqs=list(csv.DictReader(open('/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv',encoding='utf-8')))
checks={
 'REQ-001': lambda: abs(res['current_available_mw']-(res['published_mw']-res['post_publication_mw']))<1e-9 and 'adjusted for queue entries' in low,
 'REQ-002': lambda: abs(res['published_mw']-3.0)<1e-9 and '3.0 MW' in text,
 'REQ-003': lambda: ('republished' in low or 'value of record' in low) and 'map refresh' in low,
 'REQ-004': lambda: 'priority list' in low and 'refresh criteria' in low,
 'REQ-005': lambda: abs(ids['PXA-2024-0231']['capacity_mw']-1.2)<1e-9 and ids['PXA-2024-0231']['queue_date']=='2024-09-18' and 'September 18, 2024' in text,
 'REQ-006': lambda: abs(res['plan']['interim_mw']-1.8)<1e-9 and '1.8 MW' in text,
 'REQ-007': lambda: 'October 15, 2024' in text and 'reassess' in low and 'point-in-time' in low,
 'REQ-008': lambda: 'Distribution Planning' in text and '0.8 MW' in text,
 'REQ-009': lambda: feeders=={'ALN-108'},
 'REQ-010': lambda: 'Tariff §12.3' in text and 'complete' in low and 'queue position' in low,
 'REQ-011': lambda: 'Tariff §12.7' in text and 'queue order' in low,
 'REQ-012': lambda: '3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling' in text and '3.9 MW DC' in text,
 'REQ-013': lambda: 'medium-scale' in low and 'system impact study' in low and '3 MW' in text,
 'REQ-014': lambda: 'commercial small-scale' in low and '500 kW to 1 MW' in text and 'SRP-3' in text,
 'REQ-015': lambda: 'Category 3' in text and 'dedicated protection relay' in low and 'POI recloser' in text,
 'REQ-016': lambda: 'commercial small-scale' in low and '0.8 MW' in text,
 'REQ-017': lambda: 'utility-owned RTU' in text and 'SCADA telemetry' in text and 'condition of permission to operate' in low,
 'REQ-018': lambda: 'TCS-02 §5' in text and 'utility-owned RTU' in text and 'live telemetry' in low,
 'REQ-019': lambda: '10:00-16:00' in text and 'daytime-window minimum-load screen' in low,
 'REQ-020': lambda: '12 complete months of AMI interval data' in text,
 'REQ-021': lambda: 'feeder penetration' in low and 'screens' in low,
 'REQ-022': lambda: 'short-circuit' in low and 'screens' in low,
 'REQ-023': lambda: 'priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh' in low and 'refresh criteria' in low,
 'REQ-024': lambda: all(x in text for x in ['HCM-2024-Q2','PLN-ALN-108-2024-10','Tariff §12.3','DIS-01 Rev 4']),
 'REQ-025': lambda: all(x in text for x in ['HCM-2024-Q2','PLN-ALN-108-2024-10','Tariff §12.7','DIS-01 Rev 4']),
 'REQ-026': lambda: 'Tariff §12.7' in text and 'DIS-01 Rev 4' in text,
 'REQ-027': lambda: datetime.date(2025,7,14)<=datetime.date(2025,8,15),
 'REQ-028': lambda: 'UL 1741' in text and 'Control Narrative' in text and '§3.6' in text,
 'REQ-029': lambda: 'utility-owned POI recloser' in text,
}
ok(set(checks)=={r['Req_ID'] for r in reqs}, 'requirements.csv IDs do not match check mapping')
for r in reqs:
    rid=r['Req_ID']
    try:
        val=checks[rid]()
    except Exception as e:
        val=False
        print(f'ERROR checking {rid}: {e}')
    ok(val, f'failed requirement {rid}: {r["Requirement"][:120]}')

# ---- Utilisation / worst case ----
util_req=3.0/0.8
util_option=0.8/0.8

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recompute the ALN-108 pre-application capacity figure from project records."""
import json, re, datetime
from pathlib import Path
import openpyxl, docx

ROOT = Path('/filesystem')
HCM = ROOT/'Planning/Hosting_Capacity_Map_Export_2024-05-15.xlsx'
PLAN = ROOT/'Planning/2024-10-15_ALN-108_Planning_Study.docx'
ACTIVE = ROOT/'Queue/2025-07-14_Active_Queue_Report.xlsx'
ONHOLD = ROOT/'Queue/2025-07-14_On_Hold_Queue_Report.xlsx'
WITHDRAWAL = ROOT/'Queue/Withdrawal_Notice_Log.xlsx'
PUB_DATE = datetime.date(2024,5,15)
ASOF = datetime.date(2025,7,14)

def cap_to_mw(s):
    s=str(s).strip()
    m=re.match(r'([0-9.]+)\s*(MW|kW)',s,re.I)
    if not m: raise ValueError(s)
    v=float(m.group(1)); u=m.group(2).lower()
    return v if u=='mw' else v/1000.0

def read_hcm():
    wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(HCM,data_only=True)
    ws=wb['Feeder Capacity']
    for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=4,values_only=True):
        if row[0]=='ALN-108':
            return {'feeder':row[0],'substation':row[1],'voltage':row[2],
                    'published_mw':float(row[3]),'category':row[4],'last_study':row[5],
                    'publication':'05/15/2024'}
    raise SystemExit('ALN-108 row not found in HCM')

def read_plan():
    d=docx.Document(PLAN)
    text='\n'.join(p.text for p in d.paragraphs)
    m=re.search(r'Interim available capacity:\s*3\.0\s*MW\s*[-\u2212]\s*1\.2\s*MW\s*=\s*1\.8\s*MW',text)
    return {'interim_mw':1.8 if m else None,
            'postpub_queue_mw':1.2 if m else None,
            'has_1_8': '1.8 MW' in text,
            'has_1_2': '1.2 MW' in text,
            'doc_no':'PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 Rev 1',
            'date':'10/15/2024'}

def read_active():
    wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(ACTIVE,data_only=True)
    ws=wb['Active Queue']
    rows=[]
    for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2,values_only=True):
        if row[4]=='ALN-108':
            qd=row[5]
            if isinstance(qd,datetime.datetime): qd=qd.date()
            rows.append({'id':row[0],'customer':row[1],'site':row[2],
                         'capacity_raw':row[3],'capacity_mw':cap_to_mw(row[3]),
                         'feeder':row[4],'queue_date':qd.isoformat(),'status':row[6],
                         'post_publication': qd>PUB_DATE})
    return rows

def has_feeder_in_sheet(path,sheet):
    wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(path,data_only=True)
    ws=wb[sheet]
    hits=[]
    for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True):
        if any(isinstance(v,str) and v.strip()=='ALN-108' for v in row):
            hits.append(row)
    return hits

def compute():
    hcm=read_hcm(); plan=read_plan(); active=read_active()
    post=[r for r in active if r['post_publication']]
    pre=[r for r in active if not r['post_publication']]
    post_sum=round(sum(r['capacity_mw'] for r in post),6)
    current=round(hcm['published_mw']-post_sum,6)
    excess=round(3.0-current,6) if current is not None else None
    # cross-checks
    if abs(post_sum-2.2)>1e-9:
        raise SystemExit(f'Expected post-publication ALN-108 total 2.2 MW, got {post_sum}')
    if abs(current-0.8)>1e-9:
        raise SystemExit(f'Expected current capacity 0.8 MW, got {current}')
    if has_feeder_in_sheet(ONHOLD,'Holds'):
        raise SystemExit('ALN-108 unexpectedly appears in On-Hold report')
    if has_feeder_in_sheet(WITHDRAWAL,'Withdrawal Notice Log'):
        raise SystemExit('ALN-108 unexpectedly appears in Withdrawal Notice Log')
    return {'published_mw':hcm['published_mw'],'post_publication_mw':post_sum,
            'current_available_mw':current,'requested_mw':3.0,'excess_mw':excess,
            'post_publication':post,'pre_publication':pre,'hcm':hcm,'plan':plan,
            'asof':ASOF.isoformat(),'publication':PUB_DATE.isoformat()}

if __name__=='__main__':
    print(json.dumps(compute(),indent=2,default=str))

1. PURPOSE
DPS-07 establishes minimum protection requirements for the interconnection of distributed energy resources
(DER) to the Alleniom Utilities distribution system. The requirements set forth herein preserve system-side fault
clearing, prevent unintentional islanding of generation onto de-energized distribution circuits, and ensure that the
utility maintains a controllable, visible interruption point at every generating facility capable of exporting power to
the distribution network.
This standard defines the equipment, functional performance, and coordination principles applicable to protective
devices installed at the point of interconnection (POI) of an export-capable DER site. It is issued by Standards
Engineering under authority of the Director of Distribution Engineering and shall be applied to all in-scope
projects at initial screening, detailed engineering review, construction, and commissioning.
2. SCOPE
This standard applies to all distribution-connected export-capable DER sites within the Alleniom Utilities service
territory, including but not limited to:
1. Commercial small-scale DER (500 kW – 1 MW nameplate).
2. Medium-scale DER (1 MW – 5 MW nameplate).
3. Any DER of any size that is capable, by facility design or operating configuration, of exporting real power to
the distribution system through the point of common coupling.
Sub-scope DER handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application of this
standard; however, where such a facility is nonetheless configured for export, the protection principles of §4 shall
apply as adapted by the Small-Systems review.
Non-export configurations (facilities operated behind a reverse-power lockout with no export capability under any
operating condition) are outside the scope of this standard and are addressed under separate protection
guidance.
3. REFERENCES
The following documents are referenced in the application of this standard:
•
IEEE 1547 — Standard for Interconnection and Interoperability of Distributed Energy Resources with
Associated Electric Power Systems Interfaces.
•
IEEE C37.230 — Guide for Protective Relay Applications to Distribution Lines.
•
IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111 — Requirements for Overhead, Pad-Mounted, Dry-Vault, and Submersible
Automatic Circuit Reclosers.
•
ANSI C57.13 — Requirements for Instrument Transformers.

4. PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS
4.1 General
Every distribution-connected DER site subject to this standard shall be equipped with protective equipment
sufficient to accomplish, at minimum, the following:
(a) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon loss of the utility source, before the operation of any utility
reclosing sequence that would attempt to re-energize the affected circuit.
(b) Isolate the DER from the distribution system upon detection of abnormal voltage or frequency conditions on
the utility side of the point of interconnection, within the trip times required by the applicable interconnection
standard.
(c) Present the utility system operator with a visible, remotely operable, and lockable point of interruption
between the DER and the distribution circuit at all times when the DER is connected.
(d) Coordinate with upstream and downstream distribution protective devices such that a DER-side fault is
cleared by DER-side devices and a utility-side fault is cleared by utility-side devices, without unnecessary
tripping of either.
4.2 Point-of-Interconnection Recloser Requirement
Every export-capable in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned point-of-interconnection
(POI) recloser. No exceptions are specified.
The POI recloser shall satisfy the following requirements:
1. Ownership and control. The POI recloser and its associated control cabinet, communications interface,
current and voltage transformers, and control power supply shall be owned, installed, maintained, and
operated by Alleniom Utilities. The DER owner shall provide the physical site, the equipment pad, primary
conductors to the recloser terminals, and any auxiliary services (grounding, station service, communications
backhaul) as specified in the site's construction package.
2. Ratings. The recloser shall be rated for the maximum continuous current, momentary current, short-circuit
interrupting current, and system voltage of the feeder or lateral to which it is connected, with margin per
Distribution Protection Engineering's feeder-specific settings sheet.
3. Functional elements. At minimum, the recloser control shall implement the following ANSI device functions,
with settings determined per site by Distribution Protection Engineering:
— 50/51 phase and 50N/51N ground overcurrent (instantaneous and time),
— 27/59 undervoltage and overvoltage,
— 81U/81O underfrequency and overfrequency,
— 25 synchronism check for closing into an energized system,
— 32 directional power element, available for use as an export-limit enforcement or reverse-power
backstop as directed by the site's engineering determination,
— 79 automatic reclosing, enabled or blocked per the coordination scheme in §5.
4. Operability. The recloser shall be capable of local manual operation, local electrical operation from the
control cabinet, and remote operation and monitoring via the utility SCADA system per TCS-02. Loss of
communications shall not defeat local protection.
Where a referenced external standard is revised, the revision in effect on the date of the site's engineering
determination shall govern, unless Standards Engineering directs otherwise in writing.

Page 3
5. Visible break and lockout. The recloser shall provide, or be paired with, a visible-break disconnect
operable by utility personnel, with provision for utility padlocking in the open position for the purpose of
clearance holds.
6. Location. The POI recloser shall be located on the utility side of the point of interconnection, at a location
accessible to Alleniom Utilities crews 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, without transiting locked customer
premises.
4.3 DER-Side Protection
DER-side protection (generator step-up transformer protection, inverter interface protection, plant collection
protection, and any owner-installed disconnects) shall be provided by the DER owner, coordinated with the POI
recloser settings, and reviewed by Alleniom Utilities Distribution Protection Engineering prior to commissioning.
DER-side protection does not substitute for the POI recloser required under §4.2.
4.4 Grounding
The DER interconnection transformer grounding configuration shall be determined per site to be compatible with
the grounding of the connected distribution circuit, in accordance with Distribution Protection Engineering's
grounding practice memorandum for the affected feeder class.
4.5 Anti-Islanding
The DER shall be equipped with anti-islanding protection meeting the trip times and non-detection zone
requirements of the applicable interconnection standard. Passive schemes based solely on utility-side voltage
and frequency measurement are permitted only where the site's system impact study demonstrates the passive
scheme's detection performance for the range of expected islanding conditions on the connected feeder;
otherwise an active or communications-assisted scheme shall be provided.
5. COORDINATION REQUIREMENTS
5.1 Coordination with Feeder Reclosing
The POI recloser shall be coordinated with the upstream feeder recloser and any mid-line reclosers such that:
(a) The POI recloser opens on loss of the utility source before the first reclose attempt of any upstream
recloser.
(b) The POI recloser remains open and locked out until the utility source has been restored, verified stable per
the site's synchronism-check settings, and the utility system operator has authorized reconnection per the
site's operating procedure.
(c) Coordination time-current characteristics shall be documented in the site's protection coordination study
prior to energization.
5.2 Coordination with DER-Side Protection
DER-side protective devices shall clear DER-side faults without operation of the POI recloser to the extent
reasonably practicable. Where a DER-side fault is not cleared by DER-side devices within the allowable time, the
POI recloser shall trip as backup protection.
5.3 Direct Transfer Trip
Direct transfer trip (DTT) shall be applied at any site where the system impact study identifies an unacceptable
non-detection zone for anti-islanding, or where the connected feeder configuration requires supervised opening
of the POI recloser on operation of an upstream device. Where DTT is applied, the associated communications
channel shall meet the availability and monitoring requirements of TCS-02.
5.4 Reclosing Blocking
Automatic reclosing on the upstream feeder recloser may be blocked, delayed, or supervised at sites where the
DER contribution to fault current, the DER anti-islanding characteristic, or the customer load composition on the

5.5 Settings Governance
All protection settings for the POI recloser, and any changes to upstream feeder recloser settings driven by the
DER interconnection, shall be issued in writing by Distribution Protection Engineering and shall not be altered in
the field without a written revision order.
6. TESTING
6.1 Factory Acceptance
The POI recloser and its control shall be subjected to factory acceptance testing per the manufacturer's standard
test protocol and per IEEE C37.60 / IEC 62271-111, with test records delivered to Alleniom Utilities prior to
shipment.
6.2 Site Acceptance
Prior to placing the DER site in service, the following site acceptance activities shall be performed and witnessed
by Alleniom Utilities:
1. Insulation resistance and dielectric withstand testing of primary and secondary circuits.
2. Current transformer and voltage transformer ratio, polarity, and burden verification.
3. Functional testing of each enabled ANSI device function against its issued setting, including pickup, timing,
and reset.
4. End-to-end trip testing from each protection element through the recloser interrupter.
5. Verification of local and remote (SCADA) control, status, and metering per TCS-02.
6. Verification of synchronism check and reclose-block logic.
7. Verification of visible-break disconnect operation and lockout provisions.
6.3 Commissioning and Cutover
Cutover of the DER site to the distribution system shall not proceed until all §6.2 activities are complete and
accepted in writing by Alleniom Utilities. The site's initial parallel operation shall be observed by the utility system
operator with the POI recloser under active SCADA supervision.
6.4 Periodic Testing
The POI recloser shall be included in the utility's periodic recloser maintenance program. DER-side protective
devices shall be tested by the DER owner on a schedule not to exceed that of comparable utility-owned
equipment, with test records made available to Alleniom Utilities on request.
6.5 Post-Event Testing
Following any operation of the POI recloser attributable to a system disturbance, a DER-side event, or a
mis-operation, Distribution Protection Engineering shall review the event records and direct such retesting or
resetting as it determines appropriate before the site is returned to service.

§3   RTU REQUIREMENTS
§3.1   Ownership and installation
Each in-scope DER site shall be equipped with a utility-owned Remote Terminal Unit (RTU)
installed at, or immediately adjacent to, the point of interconnection. The RTU shall be procured,
owned, installed, configured, maintained, and — where required — replaced by Alleniom Utilities.
The customer shall provide the physical mounting location, environmental enclosure, station AC
service, and communications entrance conduit specified in the utility's site-specific RTU
installation drawing.
§3.3   Functional requirements
Each RTU shall, at minimum:
•
a.   Poll the DER facility's generation metering, inverter/PCS gateway, and station
instrumentation at the refresh cadence specified in §6.
•
b.   Encode and forward the required data points (§6) to the Alleniom SCADA front-end
processors over an approved communications path (§4).
•
c.   Timestamp all values to a common reference (§3.5) and buffer data locally for a minimum
of seventy-two (72) hours in the event of communications loss, with automatic backfill upon
restoration.
•
d.   Report communications status, device health, and configuration version to SCADA as
diagnostic points.
•
e.   Accept authenticated remote configuration updates and firmware from Alleniom
SCADA/EMS Engineering only.
§3.4   Environmental and station-service requirements
The RTU enclosure shall meet the environmental rating specified in the site-specific installation
drawing. Station AC service to the enclosure shall be provided by the customer through a
dedicated branch circuit backed by an uninterruptible supply sized for a minimum four (4) hour
outage ride-through, sufficient to maintain telemetry through short-duration station outages.
§3.5   Time synchronization
The RTU shall discipline its internal clock to an authoritative time source using either GNSS (GPS)
time or the Alleniom SCADA network time reference. All values reported to SCADA shall carry a
timestamp accurate to within ±1 second of UTC.
§3.6   Commissioning and end-to-end verification
§3.2   Approved models
The utility-owned RTU shall be one of the three models currently used for utility-owned RTU
service: YOT-8963, YOT-8856, or YOT-7963. Substitution is not permitted. A customer power
plant controller (PPC) may use any RTU on the plant side, provided it can communicate with the
utility-owned RTU via DNP3 (§4.2).

§7   CYBERSECURITY
§7.1   Applicability
The RTU, the communications transport between the RTU and Alleniom SCADA, and any
customer equipment that shares a physical or logical interface with the RTU are subject to this
section. Alleniom-owned assets covered here are administered under Alleniom's cyber-security
program consistent with NIST SP 800-82 and NERC CIP where applicable.
§7.2   Access control
Local and remote access to the RTU is limited to Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering and to
Alleniom-authorized service personnel. Local craft access requires two-factor authentication
against Alleniom's identity system. Passwords, shared secrets, and cryptographic keys are
managed by Alleniom and are not disclosed to the customer, developer, or any third party.
§7.3   Communications security
DNP3 Secure Authentication v5 shall be enabled where supported by the RTU. All
communications traversing any non-utility segment shall be tunneled through an
Alleniom-managed VPN using IPsec (IKEv2) with mutual certificate authentication. Certificates
shall have a maximum validity of thirteen (13) months and are rotated by Alleniom.
§7.4   Firmware, configuration, and change management
RTU firmware and configuration are updated only by Alleniom SCADA/EMS Engineering, following
the Alleniom change-management process. Firmware images shall be verified against a
cryptographic signature prior to installation. The customer shall not attempt to modify, upgrade, or
reconfigure the RTU or the utility-owned communications equipment.
§7.5   Logging and monitoring
The RTU shall log authentication events, configuration changes, communications state transitions,
and firmware operations. Logs are forwarded to Alleniom's centralized log-management system.
Anomalies detected by that system are handled per Alleniom's cyber-security incident response
procedure.

The RTU shall be housed in a locked, tamper-evident enclosure. Enclosure keys, cores, and any
physical access tokens are held by Alleniom. Physical intrusion of the enclosure shall generate a
status point (tamper alarm) reported to SCADA under §6.
§7.7   Incident response
The customer shall report, without delay, any known or suspected compromise of the RTU, its
enclosure, its communications transport, or any interface between customer equipment and
utility-owned telemetry equipment. Reports shall be directed to the Alleniom SOC and to
SCADA/EMS Engineering.
§7.8   Decommissioning
At end of life, the RTU and its cryptographic material are returned to Alleniom for secure disposal.

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.
This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.


--- page 2 ---
§2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:
(1)  Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
the affected site.
(2)  An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
exception).
(3)  The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.
Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).
§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.
The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.
Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.
The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.
Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.
Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.

The program-scope threshold is 500 kW. Facilities below 500 kW, whether commercial or residential in customer
class, are routed to the Simplified Small-Systems Process and are not administered by the DER Program.
§3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.
§3.2 Point of common coupling
The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.
§3.3 Determination on the basis of application
Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
the address of record govern.
§3.4 Aggregation
Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.
Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
resulting program-scope determination.
An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
the Company existing-DER register.
§3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.


--- page 4 ---
DIS-01 Rev 4 — Alleniom DER Interconnection Standard
Page 4
DIS-01 Rev 4 · Effective 03/01/2024
The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:
1.  Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
2.  Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.
Retrofit feasibility of legacy equipment is a factual question the Company will not decide from records alone; the
applicant or its authorized developer must confirm feasibility in writing. Absent that confirmation, the shared-POI path
under §3.5(1) is not available and the application is redirected to §3.5(2) or withdrawn.
§3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.
Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:
1.  A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
setpoint range.
2.  An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.
Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:
• Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
• POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
additional utility hardware.
Enforcement provisions apply only as the site's arrangement provides them. Their absence at a particular site does
not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.
No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.
Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
