established under TCS-02.
3.  Where §3.6 recognition is in effect at a pure-generation site with a utility POI recloser, the ANSI 32
directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips on violation.
§6 Monitoring and Control
Facilities at or above the TCS-02 program threshold shall provide real-time monitoring and control integration through
a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry as prescribed by TCS-02. Live telemetry to the Company system
operations center is a condition of permission to operate. This standard does not restate TCS-02; refer to TCS-02 §5
for the telemetry rule and to Alleniom system operations for RTU installation scheduling.
Site-level control functions required by §3.6 (Power Control System recognition), by Table 5-1 (dedicated protection
relay schemes, DER breaker arrangements), and by ERP-9 site determinations, together satisfy the
control-integration expectations of this section as applied to the specific facility.
§7 Capacity and Point-of-Interconnection Provisions
Post-execution changes to executed ISA capacity or POI require withdrawal and reapplication; ISA edits are not
permitted for capacity or POI changes.
Scope. This section governs changes proposed after an interconnection service agreement has been executed by
both parties. Prior to execution, ordinary revisions may be handled in the studies and drafting process without
invoking this section.
Principal parameters. Facility capacity and point of interconnection are principal parameters of the interconnection
service agreement. Studies, protective-equipment scoping, and queue position each depend on these parameters as
executed.
Required path. A customer or developer seeking to change either the executed capacity or the executed point of
interconnection after ISA execution shall:
1.  Submit a written request to withdraw the current application and terminate the executed ISA;
2.  File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and
3.  Accept the new queue position corresponding to the filing date of the new application.
The new application is studied on its own facts. The withdrawal-and-reapplication path applies whether the requested
change is an increase or a decrease in capacity and whether or not the requested change is characterized by the
applicant as involving new or existing equipment.
Other post-execution changes. Modifications to protective schemes, telemetry endpoints, equipment models within
the same nameplate rating, and administrative items that do not alter capacity or POI are handled under the
change-order provisions of the executed ISA and are not subject to this section.
Downstream effects. The withdrawal of an executed ISA under this section releases any related utility equipment
reservations and any related feeder headroom allocations, which are then available to subsequent applications in
queue order. Studies previously performed at the withdrawn capacity are not carried forward; the new application
receives a new study appropriate to its filed parameters.
§8 Records and Compliance
Interconnection Studies retains the application file, executed ISA, and study record for each in-scope facility for the
retention period established by Regulatory Affairs. Standards Engineering maintains the current revision of this
standard, the Certified Equipment List (CEL-2025-Q2 and subsequent editions), and the Engineering Referral
Procedure (ERP-9) register of per-site determinations.

Any conflict between this standard and the APUC-filed tariff is resolved in favor of the tariff. Any conflict between this
standard and another Alleniom operating standard encountered in screening or study is referred to per-site
engineering determination under ERP-9 §3.

Feeder ALN-108 Planning Study — Post-Publication Update Q3 2024
Alleniom Utilities — Distribution Planning
DER Program Office · 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

Doc no. PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 · Rev 1 · Date 10/15/2024 · Owner: Distribution Planning
Prepared by: June Halloway, Distribution Planning Engineer
Contact: june.halloway@alleniom.com

1. Purpose
This memorandum constitutes an interim update to the published Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map (HCM-2024-Q2, published 05/15/2024) with respect to Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine substation, 13.2 kV, pure-generation category). It is issued between scheduled quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map to record a material queue addition on the subject feeder that has occurred since the last published map release, so that Distribution Planning staff, applicant-facing correspondence, and pre-application dialogue may be informed of a working interim figure until the next full refresh cycle.
The scope of this document is limited to Feeder ALN-108. It does not modify the published values shown on any other feeder in HCM-2024-Q2, nor does it substitute for a formal feeder-level planning study in support of any specific interconnection application. Applicants and pre-application requesters seeking definitive feeder guidance for project scoping decisions should continue to consult Distribution Planning directly, and any project of consequential size on Feeder ALN-108 will require a full feeder-level planning study following the standard Alleniom Distribution Planning methodology.
2. Baseline: Published Available Capacity
The Alleniom Utilities Feeder Hosting Capacity Map was published on 05/15/2024. The map reflects, on a per-feeder basis, the published available capacity value derived from the most recent completed planning study of record for each feeder as of the publication date, incorporating recorded peak and minimum load, existing interconnected DER of record at the time of the underlying study, and standard thermal, voltage, and protection screens.
For Feeder ALN-108, the published values on HCM-2024-Q2 are as follows:
Attribute | Value
Feeder ID | ALN-108
Substation | Elderpine
Nominal voltage | 13.2 kV
DER category | Pure Generation
Last completed planning study | 04/2024
Published available capacity | 3.0 MW
Publication date | 05/15/2024


The 3.0 MW figure shown above is the baseline against which subsequent queue activity is netted for the purposes of this interim update. It remains, until the next scheduled quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map or an intervening full feeder re-study, the sole published available capacity of record for Feeder ALN-108.
3. Post-Publication Queue Activity
Distribution Planning has reviewed the Active Queue Report as of the date of this document to identify interconnection applications assigned to Feeder ALN-108 that have been queued subsequent to publication of the Hosting Capacity Map. The following post-publication queue entry has been identified on Feeder ALN-108:
Queue date | Feeder | Requested capacity (nameplate) | DER category
09/18/2024 | ALN-108 | 1.2 MW | Pure Generation


The 1.2 MW project queued on 09/18/2024 is a pure-generation interconnection request, consistent with the DER category assigned to the feeder in HCM-2024-Q2. It represents the sole queue addition on Feeder ALN-108 identified in the Active Queue Report between the publication date of the map (05/15/2024) and the date of this study.
No other pending applications, executed interconnection service agreements, or in-service DER additions on Feeder ALN-108 have been identified since publication of HCM-2024-Q2 that would materially alter the baseline figure or the interim netted position stated below.
4. Interim Netted Figure
Applying the post-publication queue entry identified in Section 3 against the published available capacity of record stated in Section 2, the interim netted available capacity figure for Feeder ALN-108 as of the date of this document is calculated as follows:
Interim available capacity: 3.0 MW − 1.2 MW = 1.8 MW.
This interim figure is provided as a working reference for Distribution Planning staff and for use in pre-application correspondence concerning Feeder ALN-108 where such correspondence is issued between quarterly refreshes of the Hosting Capacity Map. The figure is not a substitute for, and does not supersede, the published available capacity value of record on HCM-2024-Q2; the published value remains 3.0 MW until the next map republication.
The interim figure carries the following stated limitations:
It reflects the state of the queue as of the date of this document only. Any subsequent queue additions, withdrawals, or reassignments affecting Feeder ALN-108 that post-date this study are not reflected in the figure above and will require Distribution Planning to reassess the interim position accordingly.
It applies a straight-line nameplate netting against the published available capacity. A full feeder re-study, when performed, may yield a different available capacity value on Feeder ALN-108 depending on updated load recordings, revised existing-DER accounting, and the outcome of thermal, voltage, and protection screens as re-run against current data.
The 1.2 MW queue entry is at the application/queue stage. Should that application be withdrawn or should its final capacity change following study or agreement negotiation, the interim netted figure would require corresponding adjustment.
5. Recommendation
Distribution Planning recommends the following:
Distribution Planning staff should treat 1.8 MW as the working interim available capacity for Feeder ALN-108 in any pre-application dialogue, applicant correspondence, or internal scoping analysis conducted between the date of this document and the next scheduled refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. The published 3.0 MW figure on HCM-2024-Q2 remains the value of record for the map itself and should not be altered on the published map absent republication.
A refreshed feeder-level planning study for Feeder ALN-108 should be scheduled to be undertaken in advance of, and its results incorporated into, the next full quarterly refresh of the Hosting Capacity Map. Feeder ALN-108 should be included among the feeders prioritized for re-study on the criteria stated in the map front matter: application date of pending queue entries, capacity requested relative to published available headroom, and DER category (pure generation is weighted more heavily against feeder headroom than net-metering behind-the-meter interconnections at equivalent nameplate).
This document should be reissued or superseded if any further queue activity on Feeder ALN-108 arises before the next quarterly map refresh, so that the working interim figure remains accurate as of its date of issue. Distribution Planning will monitor the Active Queue Report accordingly.
Applicants inquiring about Feeder ALN-108 between the date of this document and the next scheduled map republication should be directed to Distribution Planning for confirmation of the interim position before finalizing project sizing decisions, consistent with the general applicability note carried in the front matter of HCM-2024-Q2.

Alleniom Utilities — Regulatory Affairs
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com

INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
Doc no. | RA-2025-07-01
Rev | 1
Date | 07/01/2025
Owner | Regulatory Affairs


TO: DER Program Manager
CC: Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations
Meera Vellanki, Manager, Interconnection Studies
Ivo Grantham, Manager, DER Planning Group
FROM: Harriet Ngoyi, Director, Regulatory Affairs
DATE: 07/01/2025
SUBJECT: DER Backlog Review — Program Manager Tasking

1. Confirmation of directive
This memorandum confirms and operationalizes the internal directive issued 06/27/2025 by Dana Whitcomb, Vice President, Distribution Operations (DIR-2025-0627), ordering a full backlog review of the commercial DER interconnection program. Regulatory Affairs accepts ownership of the external commitments arising from that directive and, by this memorandum, assigns the internal queue-cleanup work to the DER Program Manager.
The scope of the backlog review, as established by the VP, is the entire active, on-hold, and past-study-timeline population of the commercial DER program queue as of the anchor date. Every application is to be accounted for by name, application number, current posture, and next required action. Nothing in this memorandum reduces, expands, or alters that scope.
2. Governing deadlines
Two dates fix the outer boundary of this work and are not to be revisited without written concurrence from the VP office and Regulatory Affairs:
08/15/2025 — Response to the Alleron Municipal League. Regulatory Affairs will issue the formal written response to the League's 06/20/2025 letter. The response will be substantive and project-specific, addressing the League's five enumerated requests on behalf of the fourteen member municipalities and school districts. Regulatory Affairs is the signatory; the DER Program Manager is responsible for delivering the underlying queue accounting on which the response will rest.
09/10/2025 — APUC briefing. The queue accounting must be complete and defensible in advance of the briefing to the Alleron Public Utilities Commission's Energy Resources Division. Regulatory Affairs will not present partial data to the Commission. Any application whose disposition remains open on 09/10/2025 must have a written reason on file, not an oral one.
Any interim regulatory information request the Division may issue in advance of the briefing will be answered from the same underlying record and will not create a separate work product for the Program Manager beyond timely disposition of the affected applications.
3. Tasking of the DER Program Manager
The DER Program Manager is tasked, effective immediately, with producing the following queue-cleanup inputs. Each input is to be closed on the record — with the supporting document, tariff citation, standard, or operating guideline named in the file — before it is reported as complete.
3.1 On-hold list dispositions. Work the current on-hold population by hold-reason category. For each project, determine the correct disposition under the applicable tariff provisions and program policy, and clear holds where the underlying reason has resolved. Cross-reference hold-reason categories against the relevant queue and financial records. Business-day counts must follow the standard business-day convention.
3.2 Applications-intake corrections. Review the active queue for duplicate, ghost, and stale-status records. Where a customer has filed a new application at a site with a prior, silently abandoned filing, resolve the intake question in writing before either record is closed or merged. Queue-date assignment must follow the written policy.
3.3 Standards-conflict routing. For every project currently sitting on a standards-clarification hold, determine and execute the correct disposition under applicable program standards and operating procedures.
3.4 Equipment allocation. Convene the equipment-allocation determination for the sites that have completed construction and are awaiting utility-owned equipment. Rank the sites under the applicable equipment deployment prioritization guideline in accordance with its procedures, and match against the current supplier delivery schedule reported by SCADA/EMS Engineering.
3.5 Aggregation determinations. For applications proposing new DER at sites that may host existing generation, apply the applicable aggregation provision before finalizing program-scope routing.
3.6 Capacity verifications. For any application on abnormality hold due to a stated-vs-nameplate capacity discrepancy, verify the nameplate from the application's technical documentation and apply the applicable interconnection standard to any claimed operating limit below inverter nameplate.
3.7 Hosting-capacity corrections. Before any capacity figure from the published hosting-capacity map is communicated externally, confirm that the figure reflects the current state of the affected feeder. A priority refresh is to be requested from Distribution Planning under the published refresh-prioritization criteria.
3.8 Witness-test dispositions. Verify each inverter model against the applicable certified equipment list under the commissioning procedure in effect at the time of determination. Waiver eligibility is to be determined against the applicable certified equipment list.
3.9 Supplemental-review reversals. Review any supplemental-review determination on file for consistency with current program procedures. Where the record requires revision, update the file and flag any prior memorandum that has been superseded accordingly.
4. Reporting cadence
The DER Program Manager will provide weekly progress reports to Regulatory Affairs, with copy to the VP office, every Friday by close of business beginning 07/04/2025 and continuing through 09/12/2025. The weekly report will comprise:
counts by disposition category, aligned to the categories in §3 above;
items closed on the record during the reporting week, with the governing citation named;
exceptions requiring Regulatory Affairs or VP attention, including any project at risk of missing 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025;
forward-look for the following reporting week.
Reports are to be delivered in writing. Verbal updates do not substitute.
5. General provisions
Every disposition reached under this tasking must be tariff-defensible on the face of the file. Cite the specific tariff section, standard, operating guideline, or bulletin that supports the action. Where the record does not support the disposition on paper, the disposition is not ready and is to be held rather than reported.
Follow the noticing, payment-deadline, and hold-clearance procedures as written. Standards or procedural conflicts route through the established referral process; they are not to be resolved informally in the queue. Queue-date treatment must remain within what the tariff and program policy permit.
Regulatory Affairs will coordinate with Interconnection Studies (Meera Vellanki) on queue and notice records, and with the DER Planning Group (Ivo Grantham) on study status, on any input required for the League response or the APUC briefing. The DER Program Manager remains the single point of accountability for the queue-cleanup inputs enumerated in §3.
Escalate obstacles to Regulatory Affairs in writing and, where the obstacle bears on the 08/15/2025 or 09/10/2025 dates, to the VP office concurrently.

/s/
Harriet Ngoyi
Director, Regulatory Affairs
Alleniom Utilities
harriet.ngoyi@alleniom.com · (612) 555-0104

SECTION 12 — INTERCONNECTION OF DISTRIBUTED ENERGY
RESOURCES
§12.1 Applicability
This section governs the interconnection to Alleniom Utilities' (the “Company”) distribution system
of distributed energy resources (“DER”) within the Alleron service territory. Technical
requirements, screens, study procedures, and equipment standards referenced herein are set out
in the Company's DER Interconnection Standard (DIS-01) and companion standards, each of
which is incorporated by reference. Nothing in this section shall be construed to modify or
supersede any applicable safety, reliability, or protection requirement of the Company's
engineering standards.

§12.2 Scope of the DER Interconnection Program
The DER Interconnection Program administered under this section applies to applications for DER
interconnection at or above five hundred kilowatts (≥500 kW). Within the Program, DER shall be
classified according to the DER Interconnection Standard as follows:
(a)  Commercial small-scale DER — five hundred kilowatts to one megawatt (500 kW – 1
MW);
(b)  Medium-scale DER — one megawatt to five megawatts (1 MW – 5 MW).
The Program scope threshold is ≥500 kW. DER below five hundred kilowatts (sub-500 kW),
whether commercial or residential, are not administered under this section and shall instead be
processed under the Company's Simplified Small-Systems Process, which is filed separately
and is outside the DER Interconnection Program.
Aggregation, controlled-capacity recognition, and shared point-of-interconnection eligibility are
addressed in the DER Interconnection Standard and shall control the classification of any facility
whose nameplate rating, aggregate site rating, or point of common coupling brings it within
Program scope.

§12.3 Application Intake and Queue Position
A complete application shall establish the applicant's queue position as of the date the Company
determines the application to be complete. Applications determined to be incomplete shall be
returned with a written deficiency notice identifying each item requiring cure and the date by which
cure is required. Queue position is not transferable between applications except as expressly
provided in the DER Interconnection Standard.
§12.4 Deemed Withdrawal Following Notice of Impending Withdrawal or Cancellation
Upon issuance of a formal written Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation by the
Company, the applicant shall have thirty (30) business days from the date of the notice to submit
a substantive response curing the matter identified therein. If the applicant fails to respond within
thirty (30) business days, the application shall be deemed withdrawn and shall be closed from the
active queue without further action of the Company.
For purposes of this section, “business days” shall exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and federal
legal public holidays observed within the response window. Without limitation, the following
federal holidays falling within response windows relevant to the current filing period are recognized
as non-business days and shall not be counted:
Holiday
Observed Date
Memorial Day
05/26/2025
Juneteenth National Independence Day
06/19/2025
Independence Day
07/04/2025
The Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation shall be served in writing (certified mail or
verified electronic delivery) and shall state the date of issuance, the response deadline computed
under this section, and the consequence of non-response. The Company shall maintain a log of all
notices issued, dates of service, and dispositions.

§12.5 Construction-Payment Defaults
Where a construction work order or interconnection facilities invoice becomes payable and the
customer has not remitted the amount due, the Company shall inform the customer in writing of
the outstanding balance and shall issue a payment deadline of thirty (30) business days from
the date of that written notice.
For so long as the thirty (30) business-day payment deadline is running, the affected project shall
remain on hold in the queue and shall NOT be deemed withdrawn. The construction-payment
default procedure under this §12.5 is distinct from, and shall not be conflated with, the
deemed-withdrawal procedure under §12.4; the two mechanisms have different triggers, different
consequences, and different cure paths.
Upon receipt of full payment prior to expiration of the deadline, the Company shall promptly
release the hold and resume the affected work in queue order. If the deadline expires without
payment, the Company may pursue such remedies as are available under the applicable
Interconnection Service Agreement and this tariff, including, as a separate and subsequent step,
issuance of a Notice of Impending Withdrawal/Cancellation under §12.4.

§12.6 Interconnection Service Agreement
Interconnection service shall commence only upon execution of an Interconnection Service
Agreement (“ISA”) and the Company's written Permission to Operate. Material terms of an
executed ISA, including but not limited to nameplate facility capacity and the designated point of
interconnection, may not be modified by amendment. Post-execution changes to such material
terms require withdrawal of the affected application and re-application in accordance with the DER
Interconnection Standard.
§12.7 Nondiscriminatory Queue-Order Processing of Applications
Applications shall be processed by the Company in queue order on a nondiscriminatory basis.
No applicant shall be advanced or disadvantaged in the processing sequence by reason of
identity, affiliation, customer class, geography, or any other factor not expressly provided for in this
tariff or in the DER Interconnection Standard.
Scope note. This §12.7 applies to APPLICATION PROCESSING only — that is, to the
sequencing of screening, technical review, study assignment, and issuance of interconnection
determinations. Utility construction sequencing and the scheduling and allocation of constrained
utility-owned 
equipment

section. Such matters are addressed under the Company's operating guidelines, including OG-17
(Equipment Deployment Prioritization Guideline), which sets forth the criticality factors and
prioritization criteria applicable to constrained equipment. Nothing in this §12.7 shall be construed
to require the Company to sequence construction or equipment deployment in queue order where
OG-17 or another operating guideline provides a different criticality-based ordering.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)

ALLENIOM UTILITIES
DER Program Office
4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA · (612) 555-0100 · alleniom.com



July 14, 2025
Mr. Peter Ashford
Director of Project Development
Northline Renewables LLC
1840 Ferngate Parkway, Suite 210
Halston, Alleron 02HA

Re: Pre-Application Request dated July 2, 2025 — 3 MW Project on Feeder
ALN-108 (Elderpine Solar I)
Our reference: DER-PA-2025-ALN108-01

Dear Mr. Ashford:
Thank you for your pre-application request dated July 2, 2025 for a 3 MW pure-
generation photovoltaic project on Feeder ALN-108 in the Elderpine substation service
area. This letter responds to each of the three items in your request and states the
capacity figure the DER Program Office will apply as of July 14, 2025.

Determination
The 3.0 MW published availability on Feeder ALN-108 is not current, and the
DER Program Office cannot confirm 3.0 MW for the Elderpine Solar I project. As
of July 14, 2025, the available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a new pure-generation
interconnection is 0.8 MW. The requested 3.0 MW nameplate AC exceeds the available
capacity by 2.2 MW.
 Requested item                                       Response
 1. Written confirmation of currently available       Not confirmed at 3.0 MW. Current available
 capacity for a 3 MW pure-generation                  capacity is 0.8 MW; 3.0 MW exceeds it by 2.2
 interconnection                                      MW.
 2. Known conditions, restrictions or upgrade         No project-specific upgrade scope has been
 indications for a 3 MW project                       identified because no project study has been
                                                      performed. 3 MW is medium-scale and
                                                      requires a system impact study; the full
                                                      Category 3 protection, metering and telemetry
                                                      requirements apply.
 3. Pre-application dialogue meeting with             Offered for Tuesday, July 29, 2025, 10:00–
 Distribution Planning and the DER Program            11:00 a.m. Central, in Halston or by video
 Office                                               conference; please confirm by July 22, 2025.




       Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office | Pre-Application Response — Feeder ALN-108 | Page 1
 1. Available capacity on Feeder ALN-108
The current figure is 0.8 MW. It is derived from the published map value by applying the
adjustment method stated in the map itself and the later planning update, as follows:
 Step                                Capacity                            Record and date

 Published available capacity        3.0 MW                              HCM-2024-Q2, Feeder ALN-108
 (baseline)                                                              row, published 05/15/2024; last
                                                                         planning study 04/2024
 Less PXA-2024-0231                  −1.2 MW                             Active Queue Report
 (Grantwyck ALN-108 Field                                                07/14/2025; PLN-ALN-108-
 Solar), queued 09/18/2024                                               2024-10 Rev 1, §3
 Subtotal after the first post-      1.8 MW                              PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 Rev 1,
 publication entry                                                       §4 (10/15/2024)
 Less PXA-2025-0044                  −1.0 MW                             Active Queue Report
 (Cindermere Feeder Site A),                                             07/14/2025
 queued 02/06/2025
 Current available capacity as       0.8 MW                              3.0 − 1.2 − 1.0
 of 07/14/2025

The 3.0 MW figure is the published value of record for the map, not a current statement
of headroom. HCM-2024-Q2 states that “Published values do not reflect interconnection
queue activity recorded after the publication date” and that “A pre-application capacity
response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added
since publication.” The published value is stated as of May 15, 2024. No later edition of
the map, and no later full feeder study, is in the record as of July 14, 2025.
Distribution Planning’s October 15, 2024 interim update netted the first post-publication
entry, PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, queued September 18, 2024), producing the 1.8 MW
interim figure. That update states that any queue addition after October 15, 2024
requires reassessment. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows PXA-2025-0044
(1.0 MW, queued February 6, 2025) in technical screening on Feeder ALN-108; it is the
only ALN-108 entry added after the October 15, 2024 update. No ALN-108 application
appears on the July 14, 2025 On-Hold Queue Report, and no ALN-108 notice appears in
the Withdrawal Notice Log. The further adjustment is therefore 1.8 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW.
Two earlier ALN-108 entries — PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued November 20, 2023;
ISA executed) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued April 3, 2024; construction) — were
recorded on the feeder before the May 15, 2024 publication. They are not queue entries
added since publication; the map’s adjustment method therefore does not deduct them
from the published value, and this response does not restate the published baseline for
pre-publication queue activity. The 0.8 MW is a point-in-time, straight-line netting; it is
not a reservation and not a substitute for a full feeder study. A later withdrawal or
change of any queued project would change the figure, and a full re-study could produce
a different value after updated load, existing-DER accounting and protection screens.

2. Conditions, restrictions and upgrade indications
No project-specific Distribution Planning study has been performed for the Elderpine
Solar I project, so no project-specific upgrade scope or cost can be confirmed at this
time. A 3 MW AC project is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 3-1, and would
require initial screening and a system impact study. That study would determine the
thermal, voltage, short-circuit and protection impacts and any network upgrades
required. For classification, the governing figure is the 3.0 MW AC aggregate at the
point of common coupling under DIS-01 §3.1; the 3.9 MW DC array is not the
interconnection capacity. A lower export limit would be recognized only with a valid UL
1741 / UL 3141 Power Control System certification and an approved Control Narrative

        Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office | Pre-Application Response — Feeder ALN-108 | Page 2
 under DIS-01 §3.6; no such submissions accompanied the pre-application, so the 3 MW
nameplate governs.
Any formal application would take its queue position only when the application is
determined complete, under Tariff §12.3, and would be processed in queue order under
Tariff §12.7. The existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW) and
PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), are ahead of a new filing in the July 14,
2025 Active Queue Report. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a
queue position.
For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-
1 apply. At a minimum, the project must provide or accommodate:
   a customer-owned, lockable, visible-break DER-side disconnect;
   a dedicated protection relay, and a DER breaker with a protection relay scheme
    where specified per site by protection engineering;
   a utility-owned POI recloser, which DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 also requires for every export-
    capable in-scope site, with its ANSI 32 directional-power element available to
    enforce any controlled limit recognized under DIS-01 §3.6;
   anti-islanding by a dedicated relay scheme, with transfer trip where protection
    engineering requires it;
   a bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as the feeder configuration
    requires; and
   a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, with live
    telemetry to the System Operations Center as a condition of permission to operate.
These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.
Equipment supply is a further schedule condition. The current approved suppliers quote
approximately eight months from purchase-order acknowledgement to delivery for both
the utility-owned RTU and the POI recloser (SCADA-EQP-2025-06 Rev 1, Supplier Lead-
Time Report, June 30, 2025). A Q4 2026 in-service target should carry that procurement
period.
Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC
range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with
initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00
daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete
months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit
screens. A project in that range remains an export-capable, in-scope DER site: TCS-02
§5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before permission to
operate, and DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 requires a customer-owned lockable visible-
break DER-side disconnect and a bidirectional revenue meter. On the POI recloser,
DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 states that a POI recloser is not required, while DPS-07 Rev
2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser at every export-capable in-scope site. That
conflict is not resolved by choosing one standard: DIS-01 §8 requires it to be referred to
a per-site engineering determination under ERP-9 §3, on Form ER-11, before the
project’s protective-equipment scoping is finalized. Pending that determination, the
project should carry a utility-owned POI recloser in its planning and cost basis for this
option. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing
that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does
not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still
govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of
the current headroom.




       Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office | Pre-Application Response — Feeder ALN-108 | Page 3
 3. Pre-application dialogue meeting
We will hold a pre-application dialogue meeting on Tuesday, July 29, 2025, from
10:00 to 11:00 a.m. Central time, at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, or by video
conference if you prefer. June Halloway (Distribution Planning) and Meera Vellanki
(Manager, Interconnection Studies) will attend for Alleniom. Please confirm by July 22,
2025 and send the single-line diagram, inverter specifications, site plan and target in-
service date three business days before the meeting. If July 29 does not work, we will
offer August 5, 2025 at the same time. The meeting will cover the capacity record, the
sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.
Map maintenance. Because HCM-2024-Q2 is more than a year old and two post-
publication queue entries now affect Feeder ALN-108, Distribution Planning has placed
ALN-108 on its priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh under the map’s
refresh criteria as of the date of this letter. The published 3.0 MW remains the map
value of record until a later edition is issued; it should not be used for project sizing in
the interim. The 0.8 MW figure in this letter is the current figure for that purpose.
We recognize that 0.8 MW is materially below the 3.0 MW you used for initial scoping.
The record supports the lower figure, and we are prepared to discuss the options at the
meeting.
Please direct any questions to me at (612) 555-0105 or june.halloway@alleniom.com.

Sincerely,


June Halloway
Distribution Planning Engineer
Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
(612) 555-0105 · june.halloway@alleniom.com

[0] ALLENIOM UTILITIES

[1] DER Program Office

[2] 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com

[4] July 14, 2025

[5] Mr. Peter Ashford

[6] Director of Project Development

[7] Northline Renewables LLC

[8] 1840 Ferngate Parkway, Suite 210

[9] Halston, Alleron 02HA

[10] Re:  Pre-Application Request dated July 2, 2025 — 3 MW Project on Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine Solar I)

[11] Our reference: DER-PA-2025-ALN108-01

[12] Dear Mr. Ashford:

[13] Thank you for your pre-application request dated July 2, 2025 for a 3 MW pure-generation photovoltaic project on Feeder ALN-108 in the Elderpine substation service area. This letter responds to each of the three items in your request and states the capacity figure the DER Program Office will apply as of July 14, 2025.

[14] Determination

[15] The 3.0 MW published availability on Feeder ALN-108 is not current, and the DER Program Office cannot confirm 3.0 MW for the Elderpine Solar I project. As of July 14, 2025, the available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a new pure-generation interconnection is 0.8 MW. The requested 3.0 MW nameplate AC exceeds the available capacity by 2.2 MW.

[16] 1.  Available capacity on Feeder ALN-108

[17] The current figure is 0.8 MW. It is derived from the published map value by applying the adjustment method stated in the map itself and the later planning update, as follows:

[18] The 3.0 MW figure is the published value of record for the map, not a current statement of headroom. HCM-2024-Q2 states that “Published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date; the active-queue register maintained by the DER Program Office is the record of that activity,” and that “A pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication.” The published value is stated as of May 15, 2024. No later edition of the map and no later full feeder study are in the record as of July 14, 2025.

[19] Distribution Planning’s October 15, 2024 interim update netted the first post-publication entry, PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, queued September 18, 2024), producing the 1.8 MW interim figure. That update states that any queue addition after October 15, 2024 requires reassessment. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, queued February 6, 2025) in technical screening on Feeder ALN-108; it is the only ALN-108 entry added after the October 15, 2024 update. No ALN-108 application appears on the July 14, 2025 On-Hold Queue Report, and no ALN-108 notice appears in the Withdrawal Notice Log. The further adjustment is therefore 1.8 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW.

[20] Two earlier ALN-108 entries — PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued November 20, 2023; ISA executed) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued April 3, 2024; construction) — were recorded on the feeder before the May 15, 2024 publication. The published 3.0 MW is stated as the feeder’s available capacity as of May 15, 2024, and the map’s method adjusts that baseline only for queue entries added after that date. These two entries were already on the queue before that date and are therefore within the baseline the map states, not post-publication additions, and the adjustment method does not deduct them again. The 0.8 MW is a point-in-time, straight-line netting; it is not a reservation and not a substitute for a full feeder study. A later withdrawal or change of any queued project would change the figure, and a full re-study could produce a different value after updated load, existing-DER accounting and protection screens.

[21] 2.  Conditions, restrictions and upgrade indications

[22] No project-specific Distribution Planning study has been performed for the Elderpine Solar I project, so no project-specific upgrade scope or cost can be confirmed at this time. A 3 MW AC project is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 3-1, and would require initial screening and a system impact study. That study would determine the thermal, voltage, short-circuit and protection impacts and any network upgrades required. For classification, the governing figure is the 3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling under DIS-01 §3.1; the 3.9 MW DC array is not the interconnection capacity. A lower export limit would be recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 Power Control System certification and an approved Control Narrative under DIS-01 §3.6; no such submissions accompanied the pre-application, so the 3 MW nameplate governs.

[23] Any formal application would take its queue position only when the application is determined complete, under Tariff §12.3, and would be processed in queue order under Tariff §12.7. The existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW) and PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), are ahead of a new filing in the July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a queue position.

[24] For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply. At a minimum, the project must provide or accommodate:

[25] a customer-owned, lockable, visible-break DER-side disconnect;

[26] a dedicated protection relay, and a DER breaker with a protection relay scheme where specified per site by protection engineering;

[27] a utility-owned POI recloser, which DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 also requires for every export-capable in-scope site, with its ANSI 32 directional-power element available to enforce any controlled limit recognized under DIS-01 §3.6;

[28] anti-islanding by a dedicated relay scheme, with transfer trip where protection engineering requires it;

[29] a bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as the feeder configuration requires; and

[30] a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, with live telemetry to the System Operations Center as a condition of permission to operate.

[31] These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.

[32] Equipment supply is a further schedule condition. The current approved suppliers quote approximately eight months from purchase-order acknowledgement to delivery for both the utility-owned RTU and the POI recloser (SCADA-EQP-2025-06 Rev 1, Supplier Lead-Time Report, June 30, 2025). A Q4 2026 in-service target should carry that procurement period.

[33] Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. A project in that range remains an export-capable, in-scope DER site: TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before permission to operate, and DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 requires a customer-owned lockable visible-break DER-side disconnect and a bidirectional revenue meter. On the POI recloser, DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 states that a POI recloser is not required, while DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser at every export-capable in-scope site. That conflict is not resolved by choosing one standard: DIS-01 §8 requires it to be referred to a per-site engineering determination under ERP-9 §3, on Form ER-11, before the project’s protective-equipment scoping is finalized. Pending that determination, the project should carry a utility-owned POI recloser in its planning and cost basis for this option. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.

[34] 3.  Pre-application dialogue meeting

[35] We will hold a pre-application dialogue meeting on Tuesday, July 29, 2025, from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m. Central time, at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, or by video conference if you prefer. June Halloway (Distribution Planning) and Meera Vellanki (Manager, Interconnection Studies) will attend for Alleniom. Please confirm by July 22, 2025 and send the single-line diagram, inverter specifications, site plan and target in-service date three business days before the meeting. If July 29 does not work, we will offer August 5, 2025 at the same time. The meeting will cover the capacity record, the sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.

[36] Map maintenance. Because HCM-2024-Q2 is more than a year old and two post-publication queue entries now affect Feeder ALN-108, Distribution Planning has placed ALN-108 on its priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh under the map’s refresh criteria as of the date of this letter. The published 3.0 MW remains the map value of record until a later edition is issued; it should not be used for project sizing in the interim. The 0.8 MW figure in this letter is the current figure for that purpose.

[37] We recognize that 0.8 MW is materially below the 3.0 MW you used for initial scoping. The record supports the lower figure, and we are prepared to discuss the options at the meeting.

[38] Please direct any questions to me at (612) 555-0105 or june.halloway@alleniom.com.

[39] Sincerely,

[40] June Halloway

[41] Distribution Planning Engineer

[42] Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office

[43] (612) 555-0105  ·  june.halloway@alleniom.com

§1   Purpose
This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.
Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
judgment.
Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.
§2   Scope
This procedure applies to:
(a)  all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and
(b)  all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
MW – 5 MW).
This procedure does not apply to:
(a)  sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;
(b)  capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
governed by DIS-01 §7; or
(c)  domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.
Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.
§3   Screens


--- page 2 ---
SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure  ·  Effective 02/10/2025  ·  Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering
Page 2
Applications entering supplemental review shall be evaluated under the following screens, in the order given. An
application that fails any screen shall be considered a candidate for a study agreement; the reviewing engineer
shall document the failing screen, the underlying data, and the recommended disposition per §6.
Screen A — Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder. Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus
requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Queue
positions are those on record with the DER Program Office at the date of screen evaluation.
Screen B — Voltage regulation and flicker. Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where
none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation
performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record.
Screen C — Short-circuit contribution. DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective
device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to
fall below the values specified in DPS-07.
Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. Governed by §4.
Screen E — Reverse power flow at substation. Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the
substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in
place, the application shall be routed to study.
Passing all applicable screens is a necessary but not sufficient condition for interconnection; the application
remains subject to the balance of the DIS-01 evaluation, including protection and telemetry requirements.
§4   100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. For solar DER, the minimum load used in this screen shall be the
minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data. The absolute
overnight minimum shall NOT be used. Requested DER capacity must be ≤ this daytime-window minimum for
the site to pass the screen.
The daytime-window minimum shall be computed from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent
complete twelve (12) calendar months, aggregated to fifteen-minute intervals aligned to the feeder AMI
collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time
on the feeder. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching shall be excluded
and the exclusion documented in the reviewer's worksheet. Where fewer than twelve (12) months of AMI interval
data are available, the reviewer shall use the longest continuous complete period available and note the
data-window length in the supplemental review memo.
The daytime-window minimum determined under this section is the sole minimum-load figure used for the solar
100%-of-minimum-load screen. Feeder minimum-load figures produced for other purposes — planning studies,
hosting-capacity map inputs, protection coordination — are not substitutes for the value computed under this
section and shall not be carried into the Screen D determination without recomputation on the AMI record.
Where a prior supplemental review memo on the same feeder has applied a different minimum-load basis, the
reviewer shall recompute the value under this section and, if the two disagree, supersede the earlier memo in the
file.
§5   Data sources
The following data sources are authoritative for supplemental review under this procedure:


--- page 3 ---

(a)  Feeder AMI interval data — from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse, at the meter aggregation level
published for the subject feeder. AMI interval data is the sole authoritative source for the Screen D
minimum-load determination described in §4.
(b)  Distribution planning record — most recent feeder planning study, conductor and transformer impedance
data, and protection coordination settings, held by Distribution Planning.
(c)  DER queue — active-queue and on-hold registers maintained by the DER Program Office as of the screen
evaluation date. Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen
A.
(d)  Certified Equipment List (CEL) — current edition, for verification that proposed inverters and PCS
equipment are eligible to be considered under the screens.
(e)  Interconnection application record — the applicant's filed capacity, single-line diagram, inverter
specifications, and control narrative (where controlled-capacity operation is asserted under DIS-01 §3.6).
Substitution of a source not listed above shall be documented in the memo produced under §6, together with the
reason for the substitution.
§6   Documentation
The reviewing engineer shall produce a supplemental review memo for each application processed under this
procedure. The memo shall contain, at minimum:
(a)  application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity;
(b)  the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each;
(c)  for Screen D, the daytime-window minimum load determined per §4, the data window used, the count of
intervals evaluated, and any interval exclusions with reason;
(d)  the recommended disposition — advance without study agreement, advance to study agreement, or return to
applicant with specified deficiency;
(e)  reviewer signature and date; and
(f)  the identifiers of any earlier supplemental review memos superseded.
The memo shall be filed to the interconnection application record within five (5) business days of screen
completion. Where a memo supersedes an earlier determination on the same application or the same feeder, the
superseded memo shall be flagged in the file and a cross-reference to the superseding memo added to its cover.

No ALN-108 application appears on the July 14, 2025 On-Hold Queue Report, and no ALN-108 notice appears in the Withdrawal Notice Log. The further adjustment is therefore 1.8 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW.[size=10.5]

The published 3.0 MW is stated as the feeder’s available capacity as of May 15, 2024, and the map’s method adjusts that baseline only for queue entries added after that date. These two entries were already on the queue before that date and are therefore within the baseline the map states, not post-publication additions, and the adjustment method does not deduct them again. The 0.8 MW is a point-in-time, straight-line netting; it is not a reservation and not a substitute for a full feeder study. [body.p.21] (style=Heading 1): 2.  Conditions, restrictions and upgrade indications[size=13.0]
[body.p.22]: No project-specific Distribution Planning study has been performed for the Elderpine Solar I project, so no project-specific upgrade scope or cost can be confirmed at this time. A 3 MW AC project is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 3-1, and would require initial screening and a system impact study. That study would determine the thermal, voltage, short-circuit and protection impacts and any network upgrades required. For classification, the governing figure is the 3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling under DIS-01 §3.1; the 3.9 MW DC array is not the interconnection capacity. A lower export limit would be recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 Power Control System certification and an approved Control Narrative under DIS-01 §3.6; no such submissions accompanied the pre-application, so the 3 MW nameplate governs.[size=10.5]
[body.p.23]: Any formal application would take its queue position only when the application is determined complete, under Tariff §12.3, and would be processed in queue order under Tariff §12.7. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows the existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW) and PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), ahead of a new filing. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a queue position.[size=10.5]
[body.p.24]: For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply. At a minimum, the project must provide or accommodate:[size=10.5]
[body.p.25] (style=List Bullet): a customer-owned, lockable, visible-break DER-side disconnect;[size=10.5]
[body.p.26] (style=List Bullet): a dedicated protection relay, and a DER breaker with a protection relay scheme where specified per site by protection engineering;[size=10.5]
[body.p.27] (style=List Bullet): a utility-owned POI recloser, which DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 also requires for every export-capable in-scope site, with its ANSI 32 directional-power element available to enforce any controlled limit recognized under DIS-01 §3.6;[size=10.5]
[body.p.28] (style=List Bullet): anti-islanding by a dedicated relay scheme, with transfer trip where protection engineering requires it;[size=10.5]
[body.p.29] (style=List Bullet): a bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as the feeder configuration requires; and[size=10.5]
[body.p.30] (style=List Bullet): a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, with live telemetry to the System Operations Center as a condition of permission to operate.[size=10.5]
[body.p.31]: These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.[size=10.5]
[body.p.32]: Equipment supply is a further schedule condition. The current approved suppliers quote approximately eight months from purchase-order acknowledgement to delivery for both the utility-owned RTU and the POI recloser (SCADA-EQP-2025-06 Rev 1, Supplier Lead-Time Report, June 30, 2025). A Q4 2026 in-service target should carry that procurement period.[size=10.5]
[body.p.33]: Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. A project in that range remains an export-capable, in-scope DER site: TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before permission to operate, and DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 requires a customer-owned lockable visible-break DER-side disconnect and a bidirectional revenue meter. On the POI recloser, DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 states that a POI recloser is not required, while DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser at every export-capable in-scope site. That conflict is not resolved by choosing one standard: DIS-01 §8 requires it to be referred to a per-site engineering determination under ERP-9 §3, on Form ER-11, before the project’s protective-equipment scoping is finalized. Pending that determination, the project should carry a utility-owned POI recloser in its planning and cost basis for this option. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.[size=10.5]

[body.p.35]: We will hold a pre-application dialogue meeting on [size=10.5]**Tuesday, July 29, 2025, from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m. Central time[size=10.5]**, at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, or by video conference if you prefer. June Halloway (Distribution Planning) and Meera Vellanki (Manager, Interconnection Studies) will attend for Alleniom. Please confirm by July 22, 2025 and send the single-line diagram, inverter specifications, site plan and target in-service date three business days before the meeting. If July 29 does not work, we will offer August 5, 2025 at the same time. The meeting will cover the capacity record, the sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.[size=10.5]

The 0.8 MW figure in this letter is the current figure for that purpose.[size=10.5]

The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows the existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW) and PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), ahead of a new filing. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a queue position.[size=10.5]
[body.p.24]: For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply. At a minimum, the project must provide or accommodate:[size=10.5]
[body.p.25] (style=List Bullet): a customer-owned, lockable, visible-break DER-side disconnect;[size=10.5]
[body.p.26] (style=List Bullet): a dedicated protection relay, and a DER breaker with a protection relay scheme where specified per site by protection engineering;[size=10.5]
[body.p.27] (style=List Bullet): a utility-owned POI recloser, which DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 also requires for every export-capable in-scope site, with its ANSI 32 directional-power element available to enforce any controlled limit recognized under DIS-01 §3.6;[size=10.5]
[body.p.28] (style=List Bullet): anti-islanding by a dedicated relay scheme, with transfer trip where protection engineering requires it;[size=10.5]
[body.p.29] (style=List Bullet): a bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as the feeder configuration requires; and[size=10.5]
[body.p.30] (style=List Bullet): a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, with live telemetry to the System Operations Center as a condition of permission to operate.[size=10.5]
[body.p.31]: These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.[size=10.5]
[body.p.32]: Equipment supply is a further schedule condition. The current approved suppliers quote approximately eight months from purchase-order acknowledgement to delivery for both the utility-owned RTU and the POI recloser (SCADA-EQP-2025-06 Rev 1, Supplier Lead-Time Report, June 30, 2025). A Q4 2026 in-service target should carry that procurement period.[size=10.5]
[body.p.33]: Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. A project in that range remains an export-capable, in-scope DER site: TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before permission to operate, and DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 requires a customer-owned lockable visible-break DER-side disconnect and a bidirectional revenue meter. On the POI recloser, DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 states that a POI recloser is not required, while DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser at every export-capable in-scope site. That conflict is not resolved by choosing one standard: DIS-01 §8 requires it to be referred to a per-site engineering determination under ERP-9 §3, on Form ER-11, before the project’s protective-equipment scoping is finalized. Pending that determination, the project should carry a utility-owned POI recloser in its planning and cost basis for this option. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.[size=10.5]
[body.p.34] (style=Heading 1): 3.  Pre-application dialogue meeting[size=13.0]
[body.p.35]: We will hold a pre-application dialogue meeting on [size=10.5]**Tuesday, July 29, 2025, from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m. Central time[size=10.5]**, at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, or by video conference if you prefer. June Halloway (Distribution Planning) and Meera Vellanki (Manager, Interconnection Studies) will attend for Alleniom. Please confirm by July 22, 2025 and send the single-line diagram, inverter specifications, site plan and target in-service date three business days before the meeting. If July 29 does not work, we will offer August 5, 2025 at the same time. The meeting will cover the capacity record, the sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.[size=10.5]
[body.p.36]: **Map maintenance. [size=10.5]**Because HCM-2024-Q2 is more than a year old and two post-publication queue entries now affect Feeder ALN-108, Distribution Planning has placed ALN-108 on its priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh under the map’s refresh criteria as of the date of this letter. The published 3.0 MW remains the map value of record until a later edition is issued; it should not be used for project sizing in the interim. The 0.8 MW figure in this letter is the current figure for that purpose.[size=10.5]
[body.p.37]: We recognize that 0.8 MW is materially below the 3.0 MW you used for initial scoping. The record supports the lower figure, and we are prepared to discuss the options at the meeting.[size=10.5]
[body.p.38]: Please direct any questions to me at (612) 555-0105 or june.halloway@alleniom.com.[size=10.5]

Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. A project in that range remains an export-capable, in-scope DER site. TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before permission to operate; DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 requires a customer-owned lockable visible-break DER-side disconnect and a bidirectional revenue meter, and its Category 2 protective-function and anti-islanding requirements also apply. On the POI recloser, DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 states that a POI recloser is not required, while DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser at every export-capable in-scope site. That conflict is not resolved by choosing one standard: DIS-01 §8 requires it to be referred to a per-site engineering determination under ERP-9 §3, on Form ER-11, before the project’s protective-equipment scoping is finalized. Pending that determination, the project should carry a utility-owned POI recloser in its planning and cost basis for this option. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.

[body.p.14] (style=Heading 1): Determination[size=13.0]

[body.p.16] (style=Heading 1): 1.  Available capacity on Feeder ALN-108[size=13.0]
[body.p.17]: The current figure is 0.8 MW. It is derived from the published map value by applying the adjustment method stated in the map itself and the later planning update, as follows:[size=10.5]

| Subtotal after the first post-publication entry | 1.8 MW | PLN-ALN-108-2024-10 Rev 1, §4 (10/15/2024) |
| Less PXA-2025-0044 (Cindermere Feeder Site A), queued 02/06/2025 | −1.0 MW | Active Queue Report 07/14/2025 |
