[body.p.18]: The 3.0 MW figure is the published value of record for the map, not a current statement of headroom. HCM-2024-Q2 states: “Published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date; the active-queue register maintained by the DER Program Office is the record of that activity. A pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication.” The published value is stated as of May 15, 2024. No later edition of the map and no later full feeder study are in the record as of July 14, 2025.[size=10.5]
[body.p.19]: Distribution Planning’s October 15, 2024 interim update netted the first post-publication entry, PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, queued September 18, 2024), producing the 1.8 MW interim figure. That update states that any queue addition after October 15, 2024 requires reassessment. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, queued February 6, 2025) in technical screening on Feeder ALN-108; it is the only ALN-108 entry added after the October 15, 2024 update. No ALN-108 application appears on the July 14, 2025 On-Hold Queue Report, and no ALN-108 notice appears in the Withdrawal Notice Log. The further adjustment is therefore 1.8 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW.[size=10.5]
[body.p.20]: Two earlier ALN-108 entries — PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued November 20, 2023; ISA executed) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued April 3, 2024; construction) — were recorded on the feeder before the May 15, 2024 publication. The published 3.0 MW is stated as the feeder’s available capacity as of May 15, 2024, and the map’s method adjusts that baseline only for queue entries added after that date. These two entries were already on the queue before that date and are therefore within the baseline the map states, not post-publication additions, and the adjustment method does not deduct them again. The 0.8 MW is a point-in-time, straight-line netting; it is not a reservation and not a substitute for a full feeder study. A later withdrawal or change of any queued project would change the figure, and a full re-study could produce a different value after updated load, existing-DER accounting and protection screens.[size=10.5]
[body.p.21] (style=Heading 1): 2.  Conditions, restrictions and upgrade indications[size=13.0]
[body.p.22]: No project-specific Distribution Planning study has been performed for the Elderpine Solar I project, so no project-specific upgrade scope or cost can be confirmed at this time. A 3 MW AC project is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 3-1, and would require initial screening and a system impact study. That study would determine the thermal, voltage, short-circuit and protection impacts and any network upgrades required. For classification, the governing figure is the 3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling under DIS-01 §3.1; the 3.9 MW DC array is not the interconnection capacity. A lower export limit would be recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 Power Control System certification and an approved Control Narrative under DIS-01 §3.6; no such submissions accompanied the pre-application, so the 3 MW nameplate governs.[size=10.5]
[body.p.23]: Any formal application would take its queue position only when the application is determined complete, under Tariff §12.3, and would be processed in queue order under Tariff §12.7. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows the existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW) and PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), ahead of a new filing. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a queue position.[size=10.5]
[body.p.24]: For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply. At a minimum, the project must provide or accommodate:[size=10.5]
[body.p.25] (style=List Bullet): a customer-owned, lockable, visible-break DER-side disconnect;[size=10.5]
[body.p.26] (style=List Bullet): a dedicated protection relay, and a DER breaker with a protection relay scheme where specified per site by protection engineering;[size=10.5]
[body.p.27] (style=List Bullet): a utility-owned POI recloser, which DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 also requires for every export-capable in-scope site, with its ANSI 32 directional-power element available to enforce any controlled limit recognized under DIS-01 §3.6;[size=10.5]
[body.p.28] (style=List Bullet): anti-islanding by a dedicated relay scheme, with transfer trip where protection engineering requires it;[size=10.5]
[body.p.29] (style=List Bullet): a bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as the feeder configuration requires; and[size=10.5]
[body.p.30] (style=List Bullet): a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, with live telemetry to the System Operations Center as a condition of permission to operate.[size=10.5]
[body.p.31]: These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.[size=10.5]
[body.p.32]: Equipment supply is a further schedule condition. The current approved suppliers quote approximately eight months from purchase-order acknowledgement to delivery for both the utility-owned RTU and the POI recloser (SCADA-EQP-2025-06 Rev 1, Supplier Lead-Time Report, June 30, 2025). A Q4 2026 in-service target should carry that procurement period.[size=10.5]
[body.p.33]: Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. A project in that range remains an export-capable, in-scope DER site. TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before permission to operate; DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 requires a customer-owned lockable visible-break DER-side disconnect and a bidirectional revenue meter, and its Category 2 protective-function and anti-islanding requirements also apply. On the POI recloser, DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 states that a POI recloser is not required, while DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser at every export-capable in-scope site. That conflict is not resolved by choosing one standard: DIS-01 §8 requires it to be referred to a per-site engineering determination under ERP-9 §3, on Form ER-11, before the project’s protective-equipment scoping is finalized. Pending that determination, the project should carry a utility-owned POI recloser in its planning and cost basis for this option. Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.[size=10.5]

The meeting will cover the capacity record, the sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.[size=10.5]

0 | Normal | ALLENIOM UTILITIES

1 | Normal | DER Program Office

2 | Normal | 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, Alleron 01HA  ·  (612) 555-0100  ·  alleniom.com

4 | Normal | July 14, 2025

10 | Normal | Re:  Pre-Application Request dated July 2, 2025 — 3 MW Project on Feeder ALN-108 (Elderpine Solar I)

11 | Normal | Our reference: DER-PA-2025-ALN108-01

12 | Normal | Dear Mr. Ashford:

13 | Normal | Thank you for your pre-application request dated July 2, 2025 for a 3 MW pure-generation photovoltaic project on Feeder ALN-108 in the Elderpine substation service area. This letter responds to each of the three items in your request and states the capacity figure the DER Program Office will apply as of July 14, 2025.

14 | Heading 1 | Determination

15 | Normal | The 3.0 MW published availability on Feeder ALN-108 is not current, and the DER Program Office cannot confirm 3.0 MW for the Elderpine Solar I project. As of July 14, 2025, the available capacity on Feeder ALN-108 for a new pure-generation interconnection is 0.8 MW. The requested 3.0 MW nameplate AC exceeds the available capacity by 2.2 MW.

16 | Heading 1 | 1.  Available capacity on Feeder ALN-108

17 | Normal | The current figure is 0.8 MW. It is derived from the published map value by applying the adjustment method stated in the map itself and the later planning update, as follows:

18 | Normal | The 3.0 MW figure is the published value of record for the map, not a current statement of headroom. HCM-2024-Q2 states: “Published values do not reflect interconnection queue activity recorded after the publication date; the active-queue register maintained by the DER Program Office is the record of that activity. A pre-application capacity response is prepared against the published value as adjusted for queue entries added since publication.” The published value is stated as of May 15, 2024. No later edition of the map and no later full feeder study are in the record as of July 14, 2025.

19 | Normal | Distribution Planning’s October 15, 2024 interim update netted the first post-publication entry, PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW, queued September 18, 2024), producing the 1.8 MW interim figure. That update states that any queue addition after October 15, 2024 requires reassessment. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, queued February 6, 2025) in technical screening on Feeder ALN-108; it is the only ALN-108 entry added after the October 15, 2024 update. No ALN-108 application appears on the July 14, 2025 On-Hold Queue Report, and no ALN-108 notice appears in the Withdrawal Notice Log. The further adjustment is therefore 1.8 − 1.0 = 0.8 MW.

20 | Normal | Two earlier ALN-108 entries — PXA-2023-0894 (1.1 MW, queued November 20, 2023; ISA executed) and PXA-2024-0091 (690 kW, queued April 3, 2024; construction) — were recorded on the feeder before the May 15, 2024 publication. The published 3.0 MW is stated as the feeder’s available capacity as of May 15, 2024, and the map’s method adjusts that baseline only for queue entries added after that date. These two entries were already on the queue before that date and are therefore within the baseline the map states, not post-publication additions, and the adjustment method does not deduct them again. The 0.8 MW is a point-in-time, straight-line netting; it is not a reservation and not a substitute for a full feeder study. A later withdrawal or change of any queued project would change the figure, and a full re-study could produce a different value after updated load, existing-DER accounting and protection screens.

21 | Heading 1 | 2.  Conditions, restrictions and upgrade indications

22 | Normal | No project-specific Distribution Planning study has been performed for the Elderpine Solar I project, so no project-specific upgrade scope or cost can be confirmed at this time. A 3 MW AC project is medium-scale under DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 3-1, and would require initial screening and a system impact study. That study would determine the thermal, voltage, short-circuit and protection impacts and any network upgrades required. For classification, the governing figure is the 3.0 MW AC aggregate at the point of common coupling under DIS-01 §3.1; the 3.9 MW DC array is not the interconnection capacity. A lower export limit would be recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 Power Control System certification and an approved Control Narrative under DIS-01 §3.6; no such submissions accompanied the pre-application, so the 3 MW nameplate governs.

23 | Normal | Any formal application would take its queue position only when the application is determined complete, under Tariff §12.3, and would be processed in queue order under Tariff §12.7. The July 14, 2025 Active Queue Report shows the existing ALN-108 applications, including PXA-2024-0231 (1.2 MW) and PXA-2025-0044 (1.0 MW, technical screening), ahead of a new filing. A pre-application request does not reserve capacity or a queue position.

24 | Normal | For a 3 MW pure-generation site, the Category 3 requirements of DIS-01 Rev 4, Table 5-1 apply. At a minimum, the project must provide or accommodate:

25 | List Bullet | a customer-owned, lockable, visible-break DER-side disconnect;

26 | List Bullet | a dedicated protection relay, and a DER breaker with a protection relay scheme where specified per site by protection engineering;

27 | List Bullet | a utility-owned POI recloser, which DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 also requires for every export-capable in-scope site, with its ANSI 32 directional-power element available to enforce any controlled limit recognized under DIS-01 §3.6;

28 | List Bullet | anti-islanding by a dedicated relay scheme, with transfer trip where protection engineering requires it;

29 | List Bullet | a bidirectional revenue meter, primary or secondary as the feeder configuration requires; and

30 | List Bullet | a utility-owned RTU with SCADA telemetry under DIS-01 §6 and TCS-02 §5, with live telemetry to the System Operations Center as a condition of permission to operate.

31 | Normal | These are standard program requirements; they are not a capacity reservation.

32 | Normal | Equipment supply is a further schedule condition. The current approved suppliers quote approximately eight months from purchase-order acknowledgement to delivery for both the utility-owned RTU and the POI recloser (SCADA-EQP-2025-06 Rev 1, Supplier Lead-Time Report, June 30, 2025). A Q4 2026 in-service target should carry that procurement period.

33 | Normal | Two sizing paths are open. First, the project can be sized in the 500 kW to 0.8 MW AC range, which would place it in the commercial small-scale class (500 kW to 1 MW) with initial screening and supplemental review under SRP-3, including the 10:00–16:00 daytime-window minimum-load screen computed from the most recent 12 complete months of AMI interval data, together with the feeder penetration and short-circuit screens. A project in that range remains an export-capable, in-scope DER site. TCS-02 §5 requires a utility-owned RTU with live SCADA telemetry before permission to operate; DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 requires a customer-owned lockable visible-break DER-side disconnect and a bidirectional revenue meter, and the Category 2 protective-function and anti-islanding requirements also apply. On the POI recloser, DIS-01 Table 5-1 Category 2 states that a POI recloser is not required, while DPS-07 Rev 2 §4.2 requires a utility-owned POI recloser at every export-capable in-scope site. That conflict is not resolved by choosing one standard: DIS-01 §8 requires it to be referred to a per-site engineering determination under ERP-9 §3, on Form ER-11, before the project’s protective-equipment scoping is finalized. Pending that determination, the project should carry a utility-owned POI recloser in its planning and cost basis for this option.

34 | Normal | Second, the 3 MW project can be filed for a full system impact study, recognizing that capacity, upgrade cost and schedule are not assured. Sizing within 0.8 MW does not itself reserve that capacity, because a complete application and queue order still govern, and we recommend sizing below 0.8 MW so that the project is not at the limit of the current headroom.

35 | Heading 1 | 3.  Pre-application dialogue meeting

36 | Normal | We will hold a pre-application dialogue meeting on Tuesday, July 29, 2025, from 10:00 to 11:00 a.m. Central time, at 4200 Veldmere Boulevard, Halston, or by video conference if you prefer. June Halloway (Distribution Planning) and Meera Vellanki (Manager, Interconnection Studies) will attend for Alleniom. Please confirm by July 22, 2025 and send the single-line diagram, inverter specifications, site plan and target in-service date three business days before the meeting. If July 29 does not work, we will offer August 5, 2025 at the same time. The meeting will cover the capacity record, the sizing options and the formal application requirements; it will not reserve capacity.

37 | Normal | Map maintenance. Because HCM-2024-Q2 is more than a year old and two post-publication queue entries now affect Feeder ALN-108, Distribution Planning has placed ALN-108 on its priority list for a feeder-level re-study and map refresh under the map’s refresh criteria as of the date of this letter. The published 3.0 MW remains the map value of record until a later edition is issued; it should not be used for project sizing in the interim. The 0.8 MW figure in this letter is the current figure for that purpose.

38 | Normal | We recognize that 0.8 MW is materially below the 3.0 MW you used for initial scoping. The record supports the lower figure, and we are prepared to discuss the options at the meeting.

39 | Normal | Please direct any questions to me at (612) 555-0105 or june.halloway@alleniom.com.

40 | Normal | Sincerely,

41 | Normal | June Halloway

42 | Normal | Distribution Planning Engineer

43 | Normal | Alleniom Utilities — DER Program Office
